tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.

   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

1	# Project context
2	
3	Claude Code loads this file automatically at the start of every session in this
4	directory. It exists so a new chat does not re-litigate settled decisions or
5	redo work that was already tried and rejected.
6	
7	**Read the "Do not redo" section before proposing changes to the hero or the
8	book images.**
9	
10	---
11	
12	## What this is
13	
14	A landing page for Waqar Ahmed's one-to-one Qur'an teaching. Astro 7, hand-
15	written CSS, no UI framework. The built landing page ships ~2.4 KB of JS.
16	
17	Full documentation of how everything works is in [README.md](README.md). This
18	file is the *decision log* — the why, and the history.
19	
20	```bash
21	npm run dev      # http://localhost:4321
22	npm run build
23	npm run assets   # regenerate the book images from originals/
24	```
25	
26	---
27	
28	## Scope, as the client set it
29	
30	- **This is a landing page only.** An earlier version put every section on one
31	  page and the client pushed back hard: *"i didn't ask you to create the entire
32	  website."* `index.astro` is deliberately just `HeroStage` + `FinalCta`.
33	- `Audiences`, `Method`, `FreeTools`, `Teacher`, `Promises`, `Faq` and
34	  `Testimonials` are **finished components that are intentionally not imported**.
35	  They belong on their own pages. `index.astro` lists which page each is for.
36	- Nav and footer link lists are **empty on purpose**. A nav pointing at pages
37	  that do not exist is worse than no nav. Add entries to `links` in `Nav.astro`
38	  as pages get built and the desktop links, burger and mobile sheet return.
39	- The business model is freemium: a free practice room (Qāʿidah audio,
40	  record-and-compare, writing practice) is the next page to build.
41	  `src/pages/practice.astro` is a stub so the primary CTA does not 404.
42	
43	---
44	
45	## Do not redo these
46	
47	Each was built, reviewed by the client, and rejected. Rebuilding them wastes a
48	session and reintroduces problems that were already solved.
49	
50	### 1. Do not cross the books between themes
51	
52	Tried: dark book on the light page, ivory book on the dark page.
53	
54	It requires cutting each book out of its own background, and **every cut has an
55	edge**. Several rounds of increasingly sophisticated segmentation still left
56	visible artefacts, and the client's verdict was to go back:
57	*"the books still have the cuts, like imperfections on the edges."*
58	
59	Now each book sits on the page whose ground matches **its own photographic
60	background** — so it is not cut out at all and there is no edge to get wrong.
61	A CSS mask feathers the photo's rectangle into the page.
62	
63	The whole segmentation pipeline still exists (`scripts/cutout-books.cjs`,
64	`scripts/lib-mask.cjs`, `src/assets/*-cut.png`) and is simply not imported. It
65	is kept because it is good work and might be wanted for something else — not
66	because the crossed-books idea should be revisited.
67	
68	### 1b. Do not replace the photograph with the CSS page at rest
69	
70	Tried: the static baseline (no JS, or `prefers-reduced-motion`) showing the book
71	already **open**, so that a reader who asked for no motion still got the verse.
72	
73	The client's verdict was immediate: *"i want the images of the quran that i
74	provided."* Laying the cover open swaps his photograph for a cream CSS
75	rectangle, and the photograph is the hero — it is the thing he shot, the thing
76	the whole palette is sampled from, and the thing anyone actually came to look
77	at. The book is now **shut** at rest, with no transform on `.cover` at all, so
78	it sits pixel-for-pixel on the photograph and the book simply *is* the
79	photograph. Only scrolling ever opens it.
80	
81	The verse stays in the document behind the closed cover — read by assistive
82	technology, indexed by search — and its meaning and citation render in plain
83	text below the book, so a reduced-motion reader is not left with nothing.
84	
85	### 2. Do not put every section back on the landing page
86	
87	See Scope above.
88	
89	### 3. Do not invent content
90	
91	- **No testimonials.** `site.testimonials` is an empty array and the section
92	  does not render while empty. He has two students; fabricating reviews is out.
93	- **No credentials or bio.** Placeholder text marked `[TODO]`, rendered in
94	  visible gold so it cannot ship by accident.
95	- ~~**No Arabic on the revealed book page.**~~ **Superseded — see "The āyah"
96	  below.** The objection was to *fabricating* Qur'anic-looking script, which
97	  still stands absolutely. A real āyah, fetched verbatim and cited, is the
98	  opposite of that, and the client asked for it directly.
99	- **No region advertising on the page.** *"it is open for all, we can do seo for
100	  targetting."* `site.regions` feeds `areaServed` in the structured data only.
101	
102	---
103	
104	## The āyah
105	
106	The book opens onto **Al-Muzzammil 73:4**, set on the page in Amiri Quran, with
107	its meaning and citation below the book.
108	
109	- **The verse is the point of the whole sequence.** It contains *warattil-il-
110	  Qur'āna tartīlā* — the command to recite slowly and distinctly. That is the
111	  Qur'an's own instruction to do the thing these lessons exist to teach, and it
112	  answers the headline. It is not decoration that happens to be text.
113	- **The Arabic was fetched verbatim** from the Uthmani text at alquran.cloud,
114	  not typed from memory. If it is ever changed, copy from a trusted source
115	  rather than retyping — a dropped sukūn or a hamza on the wrong seat is a real
116	  error. It lives in `site.ayah` and nowhere else.
117	- **The translation is Yusuf Ali (1934)**, chosen because it is out of
118	  copyright. Saheeh International is not; do not paste it in.
119	- **How it is treated, deliberately:** it fades in as one piece and then holds
120	  still — it is the only element in the sequence that never moves. No per-word
121	  stagger, no letter-by-letter reveal, no parallax. It always carries its
122	  citation. The translation sits *below* the book, not on the paper, because a
123	  muṣḥaf page carries Arabic and a gloss belongs in the margin.
124	- **Ink, not gold.** Qur'anic text in a muṣḥaf is black ink; gold is for the
125	  ornament and the āyah marker. `--page-ink` is defined once and is not
126	  redefined for dark mode, because the page stays paper in both themes.
127	- **A line of our own copy was cut** to make room: "Open it with someone who can
128	  hear every letter." Three text blocks under the book crowded the moment, and
129	  that line restated the headline. `site.stage` says how to put it back.
130	
131	There is a fourth act in the sequence now — `approach` — because the book at
132	rest is too small to read a verse on. Do not remove it and leave the verse at
133	the old size; it was illegible, which is why the act exists.
134	
135	## Decisions worth keeping
136	
137	- **Astro**, chosen because the client's stated priority was SEO and reach:
138	  near-zero JS, trivial multi-page, free hosting anywhere.
139	- **Three hues only: ink, ivory, gold.** A fourth would cheapen it. Gold has
140	  three roles (`--gold-ink` for small text, `--gold` for large text and icons,
141	  `--gold-deco` for ornament) because one value cannot clear 4.5:1 at every size
142	  on a light ground.
143	- **The hero grounds are sampled from the photographs** and are load-bearing:
144	  `#EDE8DD → #E3DBCC` light, `#322B27 → #3B332D` dark. Change them and the book
145	  stops blending into the page.
146	- **Theme default is the system setting**, with a toggle that wins in both
147	  directions. Mode changes crossfade via View Transitions (700ms), with a
148	  colour-fade fallback for Firefox.
149	- **The Rub el Hizb (۞)** is the brand mark — the symbol that marks quarter-hizb
150	  divisions in a muṣḥaf, so it belongs to the subject rather than being borrowed
151	  ornament.
152	- **Icons are hand-drawn** on one 24px grid in `src/components/icon-paths.ts`.
153	  A mistyped name fails the build with a list of valid ones rather than
154	  rendering an empty `<svg>`.
155	- **Dev panel** (`DevPanel.astro`) is gated on `import.meta.env.DEV` and is
156	  verified absent from production builds. It is the client's tool for tuning
157	  values live.
158	
159	---
160	
161	## Gotchas that cost real time
162	
163	- **The dev server serves stale CSS.** This bit us repeatedly — a change looks
164	  broken in the browser but is correct in the source and in `dist`. If computed
165	  styles disagree with the file, **restart the dev server** before debugging
166	  anything else.
167	- **The dev server also serves stale *images*.** Same failure, worse symptom.
168	  Astro caches processed images in `node_modules/.astro/assets`, and that cache
169	  is not invalidated when `npm run assets` rewrites `src/assets/*.jpg`. The
170	  result: the dev preview shows the **"I am Sorry !!!!!" stamp** while `dist` is
171	  clean. Verified once by scanning both — dev had a 0..129 spread in the corner,
172	  `dist` had 49..54. Do not go hunting through `prepare-books.cjs`; delete the
173	  cache and restart:
174	  `rm -rf node_modules/.astro && npm run dev`.
175	  Trust `dist`, not the dev server, when judging an image.
176	- **PowerShell 5.1 writes a BOM** with `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8`, which
177	  corrupts `.astro` frontmatter. Use
178	  `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($p, $c, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false)))`.
179	  Likewise `Get-Content` without `-Encoding UTF8` mangles non-ASCII on display —
180	  the file is usually fine, the console is lying.
181	- **Astro scopes styles per component.** A class passed *into* a child component
182	  (`<Icon class="foo">`) is never matched by the parent's scoped CSS. Use
183	  `:global(.foo)`. This silently broke the theme toggle, the FAQ caret and the
184	  monogram before it was spotted.
185	- **`ch` units resolve against the element's own font size.** A wrapper that
186	  inherits 16px but contains display-size text will collapse to a narrow column.
187	  Put the font-size on the element carrying the `ch` measure, or use `rem`.
188	- **Author `display` beats the UA's `dialog:not([open]) { display: none }`.**
189	  Setting `display: flex` on a bare `.sheet` left a closed dialog on the page
190	  with seven keyboard-focusable links in it.
191	- **This automated browser reports `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`** and its
192	  preview pane is often `visibilityState: hidden`. So scroll animations and View
193	  Transitions do not run there by default. To verify motion work you must
194	  temporarily lift the guard, test, then restore it — and say so honestly rather
195	  than claiming to have watched something you could not see.
196	- **`src/assets/*.jpg` reverted itself once** to a pre-cleanup copy, silently
197	  reintroducing a defect. Everything is now regenerable from `originals/` via
198	  `npm run assets`, which verifies its own output.
199	
200	---
201	
202	## The photographs
203	
204	`originals/` holds two untouched files and is never written to.
205	
206	**Both originals have "I am Sorry !!!!!" stamped into the bottom-left corner** —
207	near-black on the velvet ground, near-white on the ivory one. Invisible at a
208	glance, but real pixels that show on a bright screen and in link previews.
209	`scripts/prepare-books.cjs` removes it and verifies the result, printing `clean`
210	or `STILL STAMPED`. Never ship an asset that has not been through it.
211	
212	**Known limitation:** the ivory original is only 768px wide — roughly half the
213	velvet's real detail. Its served widths are capped at 900px because beyond that
214	the pixels are upscaled invention. If a higher-resolution ivory photo ever turns
215	up, drop it in `originals/` and re-run `npm run assets`.
216	
217	Geometry, measured by `scripts/measure-book.cjs` and agreeing across both photos
218	to within 0.6%: book at x 16.25%–83.5%, y 12%–88%, cover/spine boundary at
219	76.8%. These are Arabic bindings — spine on the **right**, cover swings right.
220	
221	---
222	
223	## Still outstanding
224	
225	The client has to supply these; they render as visible gold `[TODO]` markers:
226	
227	0. **Confirm the āyah** — whether 73:4 is the verse he wants, and that he is
228	   content with scripture appearing in a scroll interaction at all. Worth asking
229	   whoever he would normally ask. One line in `site.ts` either way.
230	1. Real academy/brand name (placeholder: "Sakīnah Qur'an")
231	2. Real domain — in `site.ts` **and** `astro.config.mjs`
232	3. Email and/or WhatsApp number — without one the page cannot convert anyone
233	4. Bio and qualifications
234	5. Lesson length, price, time zones, whether he teaches girls
235	6. Regenerate `public/og.jpg` after the name changes
236	
237	Next build: the free practice room at `/practice`.
238

- **PowerShell 5.1 writes a BOM** with `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8`, which
  corrupts `.astro` frontmatter. Use
  `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($p, $c, (New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false)))`.
  Likewise `Get-Content` without `-Encoding UTF8` mangles non-ASCII on display —
  the file is usually fine, the console is lying.
- **Astro scopes styles per component.** A class passed *into* a child component
  (`<Icon class="foo">`) is never matched by the parent's scoped CSS. Use
  `:global(.foo)`. This silently broke the theme toggle, the FAQ caret and the
  monogram before it was spotted.
- **`ch` units resolve against the element's own font size.** A wrapper that
  inherits 16px but contains display-size text will collapse to a narrow column.
  Put the font-size on the element carrying the `ch` measure, or use `rem`.
- **Author `display` beats the UA's `dialog:not([open]) { display: none }`.**
  Setting `display: flex` on a bare `.sheet` left a closed dialog on the page
  with seven keyboard-focusable links in it.
- **This automated browser reports `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`** and its
  preview pane is often `visibilityState: hidden`. So scroll animations and View
  Transitions do not run there by default. To verify motion work you must
  temporarily lift the guard, test, then restore it — and say so honestly rather
  than claiming to have watched something you could not see.
- **`src/assets/*.jpg` reverted itself once** to a pre-cleanup copy, silently
  reintroducing a defect. Everything is now regenerable from `originals/` via
  `npm run assets`, which verifies its own output.

---

## The photographs

`originals/` holds two untouched files and is never written to.

**Both originals have "I am Sorry !!!!!" stamped into the bottom-left corner** —
near-black on the velvet ground, near-white on the ivory one. Invisible at a
glance, but real pixels that show on a bright screen and in link previews.
`scripts/prepare-books.cjs` removes it and verifies the result, printing `clean`
or `STILL STAMPED`. Never ship an asset that has not been through it.

**Known limitation:** the ivory original is only 768px wide — roughly half the
velvet's real detail. Its served widths are capped at 900px because beyond that
the pixels are upscaled invention. If a higher-resolution ivory photo ever turns
up, drop it in `originals/` and re-run `npm run assets`.

Geometry, measured by `scripts/measure-book.cjs` and agreeing across both photos
to within 0.6%: book at x 16.25%–83.5%, y 12%–88%, cover/spine boundary at
76.8%. These are Arabic bindings — spine on the **right**, cover swings right.

---

## Still outstanding

The client has to supply these; they render as visible gold `[TODO]` markers:

0. **Confirm the āyah** — whether 73:4 is the verse he wants, and that he is
   content with scripture appearing in a scroll interaction at all. Worth asking
   whoever he would normally ask. One line in `site.ts` either way.
1. Real academy/brand name (placeholder: "Sakīnah Qur'an")
2. Real domain — in `site.ts` **and** `astro.config.mjs`
3. Email and/or WhatsApp number — without one the page cannot convert anyone
4. Bio and qualifications
5. Lesson length, price, time zones, whether he teaches girls
6. Regenerate `public/og.jpg` after the name changes

Next build: the free practice room at `/practice`.

334	 - Ihsan (excellence in worship/practice — speaks to teaching

336	 - Tanzil (another name for the Qur'an — "revelation")
337	 - Rawdah ("garden" — references the Rawdah in the Prophet's
338	   Mosque, associated with learning and blessing)
339	
340	Domain availability not yet checked — teacher to verify via a
341	real registrar tool (Namecheap / Instant Domain Search) once a
342	name is shortlisted. Do not assume any of the above are available
343	until confirmed.
344	
345	## 20. OPEN DECISIONS CHECKLIST (fill in before/during Phase 1)
346	[ ] Final business name and logo/wordmark
347	[ ] Color palette / visual identity
348	[ ] Number of real lessons + their letter groupings (currently
349	    6 shown as example, real Qaida likely ~20)
350	[ ] Payment approach for launch (bank transfer is fine — just
351	    confirm, don't leave undecided)
352	[ ] 3D animation exact state values (section 11) — or explicitly
353	    decide to launch Phase 1 WITHOUT the animation and add it in
354	    Phase 2
355	[ ] What you prepared in advance (assets/images/notes) — confirm
356	    format and fold into this document before the first Claude
357	    Code session
358	
359	END OF REQUIREMENTS

opens and drifts left, then as it finishes opening it recenters,
and an ayah fades in.

STATUS: Working directional prototype already built (Three.js,
vertical open + fade-in ayah) — does NOT yet include the idle
float or the left-drift-then-recenter motion described below.
This needs to be rebuilt/extended, not started from zero.

STATE-BY-STATE SPEC (fill in real numbers before/during build —
these are still open):
 State A (idle, 0% scroll): closed, vertical, floating with
   ambient drift in all directions. Position: [TBD]
 State B (~0-40% scroll): cover opens, book drifts left.
   Exact rotation / offset: [TBD]
 State C (~40-80% scroll): opens further, still left of center.
   [TBD]
 State D (~80-100% scroll): fully open, recenters, ayah fades in.
   Text behavior (fade/slide/scale): [TBD]

ASSET APPROACH — decide before or during Phase 2:
 a) Procedural (canvas-drawn cover/pages on a 3D box) — already
    how the current prototype works. Fastest, least "real."
 b) Real cover art — original design or commissioned illustration.
    Claude Design is a good fit for mocking up states A-D as
    still images first, before any animation code is touched.
 c) Photographed/scanned physical Quran — LAST PRIORITY. A flat
    photo/scan of cover + a page is usable as a texture with low
    effort. A true photogrammetry-scanned 3D book is real extra
    work — avoid unless the flat-texture version genuinely isn't
    enough.
    NOTE: Qur'an TEXT is not copyrighted. A SPECIFIC PUBLISHER'S
    cover art/layout/typesetting CAN be. Fine for private
    reference; use original/openly-licensed art for anything
    public-facing.

TOOLING: Three.js (already in use) vs. CSS 3D transforms
(lighter, simpler, less real-feeling depth). Three.js is the
sensible continuation given the existing prototype.

OTHER OPEN DECISIONS:
 - Ayah logic: random per visit / fixed / daily rotation?
 - Mobile fallback behavior — needs a simplified version, decide
   what "simplified" means (static image? shorter motion range?)
 - Performance budget — must never slow down the free Qaida
   content itself, which is the actual acquisition priority

## 12. ASSETS TO SOURCE OR GENERATE
This is the practical shopping list — sort by what blocks Phase 1
vs later phases.

BLOCKS PHASE 1 (core site, no animation yet):
 [ ] Real audio recordings — native reciter reading each letter
     (minimum: all individual huroof; ideally short example words
     too, later)
 [ ] Practice sheet designs/scans for each lesson (PDF or image)
 [ ] Your photo + real bio text for the About page
 [ ] Real WhatsApp number + email for the booking handoff
 [ ] First 2-3 blog posts written (even roughly) for SEO seeding
 [ ] Business name + simple wordmark/logo decision

PHASE 2 (3D animation):
 [x] Cover art (image) — cream/gold reference on hand, flat-crop
     version still needed (see section 18)
 [ ] Video assets — DEFERRED. Claude Code writes the generation
     prompts once scene requirements are known (see section 12).
     Not a blocker for starting Phase 2 scene work.
 [ ] Final ayah text set for the reveal (a handful chosen up front,
     or all planned for rotation)
 [ ] Any supporting imagery for the hero if the book isn't the
     only visual element

PHASE 3+ (recognition features, not needed for launch):
 [ ] Training/reference data for handwriting recognition (later)
 [ ] Reference audio dataset for pronunciation recognition (later)

ON IMAGE VS VIDEO ASSET SOURCING:
Still images are handled — teacher has the cream/gold cover
reference (see section 18) and is sourcing/generating stills
directly.

Video has been difficult to produce directly, so video prompting
is DEFERRED to Claude Code: once the 3D scene and motion states
(section 11) are actually being built, Claude Code should write
the detailed generation prompts for any video assets needed
(exact framing, duration, loopability, resolution, format),
informed by what the scene technically requires — rather than the
teacher guessing at prompts in advance without that context. Do
not attempt to pre-produce video assets before this handoff; wait
until Claude Code specifies exactly what's needed and why.

## 13. WHAT'S ALREADY BUILT (DON'T REBUILD FROM SCRATCH)
 - Full styled single-page landing page (colors chosen) — v1
 - Six-page wireframe set, structure-only, animation placeholder
   marked on home (index, qaida, lesson, book, about, blog)
 - qaida.html + lesson.html upgraded with: writing canvas,
   audio playback placeholder, localStorage completion tracking,
   checkmarks on hub, optional-account messaging
 - book.html — working WhatsApp/email handoff form logic
 - Working 3D scroll-open book prototype (Three.js) — vertical
   open + fade-in ayah, does not yet include idle float or
   left-drift motion

Hand all of these files to Claude Code as a starting point —
the goal is to merge/extend them into the real Next.js app, not
start over.

## 14. SUGGESTED BUILD PHASES
PHASE 1 — Core site, no animation, no recognition AI:
 Next.js setup, 6 page templates wired to real content, writing
 canvas + real audio, booking form live, blog seeded, deployed
 and crawlable. This alone is a usable, launchable product.

PHASE 2 — 3D scroll animation:
 Extend the existing Three.js prototype with idle float + left-
 drift-then-recenter motion, real or improved cover art, mobile
 fallback, performance tuning.

PHASE 3 — Optional account system + payments:
 Magic-link auth, cross-device progress sync, Wise/Payoneer (or
 re-evaluate Stripe) integration — only once volume justifies it.

PHASE 4 — Recognition AI:
 Handwriting recognition (letters -> words -> harakat), then
 pronunciation recognition, in that order.

Do not try to scope Claude Code work for all four phases at once
— brief it on Phase 1, get something real, then move to Phase 2.

## 15. LESSON CONTENT (CURRICULUM)
The real lesson-by-lesson structure lives in `lesson-plan.csv` in
this same project folder — one row per lesson (number, title,
letters/content covered, teacher notes, difficulty). This is the
actual source of truth for what each lesson page renders. If that
file is still empty or partially filled, ask the teacher to
complete it before building out lesson content — do not invent
lesson content.

## 16. MEDIA ASSETS ON HAND
IMAGES: Black/white (light/dark mode) Qur'an cover images exist
(location: [add folder path once placed in project]). Before
wiring these into the 3D scene or hero section: confirm background
is transparent (not a white/black rectangle), confirm resolution
is high enough for a close-camera 3D texture (roughly 1500-2000px
on the long edge as a floor). See section 18 for the specific
flat-crop requirement for the 3D mesh texture vs. the angled hero
reference shot.

VIDEO: Not yet produced — teacher had difficulty generating these
directly. Per section 12, video prompt-writing is now Claude
Code's responsibility once the 3D scene's exact needs are known
(framing, duration, format). Do not treat video as a Phase 1
blocker — proceed with images/procedural assets first, add video
once Claude Code has specified what's actually needed.

## 18. VISUAL DIRECTION (REFERENCE ESTABLISHED)
Teacher has a reference cover image: cream/ivory leather, gold-
embossed ornamental border and central medallion, warm studio
lighting. This supersedes the earlier emerald-green + gold
placeholder palette used in the first colored mockup — ivory/gold
is the real direction, at least for light mode.

Dark mode counterpart: black leather + gold (teacher has this in
progress — confirm consistency with the cream/gold version once
both exist: same border pattern, same medallion design, same gold
tone, just swapped base material color).

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENT — flag before using in the 3D scene:
The existing reference image is shot at an angle with baked-in
shadow and background — good as a hero/marketing still, but NOT
usable directly as a texture on the procedural 3D book (would
look warped/double-shadowed once lit by the scene's own lights).
Need a separate flat, straight-on, front-face-only crop with no
perspective, no shadow, and a transparent or solid background,
at roughly 1500-2000px on the long edge, for actual texture use.
Request this specifically when generating/sourcing final art —
don't reuse the angled hero shot for the mesh.

## 19. NAME CANDIDATES UNDER CONSIDERATION (NOT DECIDED)
"Huroof" and "Makhraj" both rejected — Huroof too generic (just
means "letters"), Makhraj too narrowly technical for a whole
brand. Teacher wants something Islamic but broader. Candidates
still open, none chosen yet:
 - Iqra ("Read" — the first revealed word; strong thematic fit,
   but check for oversaturation, common name for Islamic schools)
 - Noor ("light")
 - Ihsan (excellence in worship/practice — speaks to teaching
   quality more than reading specifically)
 - Tanzil (another name for the Qur'an — "revelation")
 - Rawdah ("garden" — references the Rawdah in the Prophet's
   Mosque, associated with learning and blessing)

Domain availability not yet checked — teacher to verify via a
real registrar tool (Namecheap / Instant Domain Search) once a
name is shortlisted. Do not assume any of the above are available
until confirmed.

## 20. OPEN DECISIONS CHECKLIST (fill in before/during Phase 1)
[ ] Final business name and logo/wordmark
[ ] Color palette / visual identity
[ ] Number of real lessons + their letter groupings (currently
    6 shown as example, real Qaida likely ~20)
[ ] Payment approach for launch (bank transfer is fine — just
    confirm, don't leave undecided)
[ ] 3D animation exact state values (section 11) — or explicitly
    decide to launch Phase 1 WITHOUT the animation and add it in
    Phase 2
[ ] What you prepared in advance (assets/images/notes) — confirm
    format and fold into this document before the first Claude
    Code session

END OF REQUIREMENTS

1	# Quran Landing Page — Project Plan
2	
3	## Goal
4	A $10,000-quality landing page for a Quran website — a pure visual "hook," not the full site. Everything beyond the landing page is out of scope until this phase is locked and built.
5	
6	## Why this approach (history)
7	- **Attempt 1:** Full site research (page/media structure), hardcoded directly in Opus. Effort got diluted across too much scope at once — came out wrong.
8	- **Attempt 2:** Landing-page-only, user-supplied Quran images. Turned into one crammed single-page app with no real design system behind it — looked cheap, not "like a Claude website."
9	- **Attempt 3 (this plan):** Claude plans phase-by-phase here first. Each phase is locked before the next starts. User pastes each locked phase into Opus ("ultracode" = Claude run at max effort, not a separate tool) to hardcode.
10	
11	## Stack
12	Plain HTML/CSS/JS. No build tools, no framework — so each phase can be pasted in and seen working immediately.
13	
14	## Hero concept
15	Scroll-scrubbed animation: as the user scrolls, the Quran visually opens (cover lifts / pages part) — Apple product-page style, scroll position drives playback, not autoplay.
16	- Static hero image generated by AI first (this phase).
17	- Video/animation frames generated in a later phase — **hold off on video prompts until user confirms that phase has started.**
18	- User has Google Pro (Imagen/Veo via Gemini) — generation prompts should target that toolset.
19	
20	## Hard constraint: AI + Arabic text
21	AI image/video generators reliably mangle Arabic script. Any visual needing legible Quranic verse text must use real photography/calligraphy instead. AI generation is fine for the Quran object itself and for atmospheric elements (light, dust, geometric motion, texture) as long as no readable verse text is required in the render.
22	
23	## Design direction
24	Elegant, simple, built for a lasting/memorable impression — not maximalist or feature-crowded. Must support **both light and dark mode properly** (dark is not just an inverted light mode).
25	
26	Full palette, typography, spacing, motion spec, and pre-delivery checklist: [design-system/quran-landing/MASTER.md](design-system/quran-landing/MASTER.md) — generated + persisted via the `ui-ux-pro-max` skill (real database query, not invented), with a hand-derived dark-mode palette layered on top since the tool only returns one fixed palette per query.
27	
28	- **Palette:** Primary near-black `#1C1917`, background `#FAFAF9`, gold accent `#A16207` (light) / `#D4AF37` (dark) — "Premium black + gold."
29	- **Typography:** Bodoni Moda (headings) + Jost (body) — luxury/minimalist/refined pairing.
30	- **Hero opening mechanic (RESTORED 2026-09-13):** the cover lifts from its free edge and swings on the spine. It must NOT split symmetrically from the centre.
31	
32	  **This rule was reversed and then reinstated the same day.** A centre split was tried at the user's request, built, and rejected on sight: *"how can a book magically open from the center when its spine is on the right."* There is no hinge at the centre of a bound book, so the motion reads as fake no matter how cleanly it is executed. Treat this rule as settled and do not reopen it — the prototype that proved it is at `hero-prototype.html`.
33	
34	- **The book must translate as it opens.** Closed, the book occupies width W. The cover pivots on the right-hand spine and swings rightward, so when open the pair spans 2W — the growth is entirely to the **right**. Left unhandled, the book slides off-centre as it opens.
35	
36	  **Fix — put the spine at the exact centre of the generated frame, and do the recentring in CSS.** The generation keeps a dead-locked camera (no pan, no zoom, nothing for the model to drift); the element is then translated on scroll from `+W/2` (closed book reads centred) to `0` (open spread reads centred). This is the "move it" the user asked for, kept in code where it stays tunable instead of baked into footage.
37	
38	- **Inside of the front cover = plain cream endpaper.** Never a mirrored or reversed copy of the front calligraphy, never the roundel showing through. With the inside cream, the open state reads as a proper two-page spread.
39	- **Hero pose (corrected 2026-09-12):** book stands upright, front cover facing the camera nearly head-on — not lying flat / not a three-quarter table-top shot. Spine is a vertical edge on the right side of frame, page edge on the left.
40	- **Opening direction (corrected 2026-09-12 — earlier entries had this backwards):** the cover swings **left to right**. The spine is on the right, so the *free* edge is on the left; it lifts and sweeps rightward, pivoting on the right-hand spine. This is the mirror of a Western book. Do not confuse it with Arabic *reading* direction, which is right-to-left — the text flows RTL while the physical page motion goes LTR. Conflating the two is what produced the earlier error.
41	- **Working order:** perfecting the dark-mode hero image alone first; light-mode variant comes after dark is locked.
42	
43	### Asset principle (locked 2026-09-12) — applies to every generated image and video
44	Generate **clean flat assets, not finished photographs.** No baked-in tilt, perspective, directional lighting, cast shadows, vignette, glow, or particles. Straight-on orthographic front view, evenly lit corner to corner, flat solid background, tight crop.
45	
46	**Why:** baked-in lighting and perspective can't be re-themed between light and dark mode, and a tilted source fights the scroll-open animation. Glow, shadows, atmospheric particles, and depth are built in CSS/canvas at implementation time — animatable, themeable, and far lighter than shipping two moody photographs. The generated asset is the book; the hero section is composed around it in code.
47	
48	**Flat means flat:** no page edges visible on the left, no spine edge visible on the right, no book thickness at all — only the rectangular cover face. If either edge is visible, there is still rotation in the image.
49	
50	**Cover colourway (locked):** near-black / deep espresso leather with antique gold tooling — not mid-brown. Chosen so the asset sits natively on the `#1C1917` dark ground with `#D4AF37` gold, per the design system.
51	
52	**Cover design language (locked 2026-09-12, from user reference):** restrained and minimal, not densely ornate. Black field with subtle low-relief tone-on-tone texture, one thin gold double-rule border inset from the edges, single small gold roundel centred. Sparing gold. The earlier heavily-tooled arabesque direction is rejected as too busy.
53	
54	**Calligraphy (revised 2026-09-12):** the centre roundel carries القرآن الكريم, generated directly in the image. This short phrase appears on a huge number of real covers and renders acceptably; the earlier blanket "never generate Arabic" rule was too strict for it. Verify the glyphs by eye before shipping — subtle malformation is the failure mode.
55	
56	Longer or less common Arabic — the scrolling aayat above all — still must be live text, never generated artwork.
57	
58	**Orientation — two separate things, state both every time:**
59	- **Canvas:** landscape 16:9 (approved black asset is 2816×1536). Never a portrait canvas.
60	- **Book:** portrait, roughly 2:3, centred in that landscape canvas with empty background either side, whole and uncropped.
61	
62	Conflating these produced a mismatched pair once already — the white variant came back as a tight portrait crop (1846×2304).
63	
64	**Asset pair (locked 2026-09-12):** dark-mode cover approved. The light-mode cover is the same asset in ivory-white with gold — identical composition, proportions, border, roundel placement and framing, colourway only. Not a horizontal flip; spine side stays consistent. The two must stay pixel-compatible so toggling theme swaps the image without shifting layout.
65	
66	**Output size:** roughly 1200–1600px tall is plenty for a hero asset; convert to WebP for the build (the design system checklist requires WebP/AVIF). No need for huge multi-MB generations.
67	- **Aayat on scroll:** 3-4 different verses should appear/cycle as the user scrolls the hero. This text must be real type (HTML/CSS text or a proper Arabic font), never baked into the AI-generated image or video — same reason AI can't render legible Arabic script reliably. The static hero image and generated video stay text-free; verse overlays are a separate live-text layer built in Phase 5.
68	- The design system's suggested page "Pattern" (multi-chapter problem/journey/solution) does not fit this brief — only its motion, accessibility, and anti-pattern rules apply, not its section structure.
69	
70	## Tooling installed (this folder)
71	- `design-taste-frontend`, `full-output-enforcement`, `high-end-visual-design`, `image-to-code`, `imagegen-frontend-web`, `minimalist-ui` — from Leonxlnx/taste-skill
72	- `ui-ux-pro-max` — design-system skill (palettes, font pairings, UX rules)
73	- `web-design-guidelines` — audit skill, to be used once a draft exists to check
74	
75	## Phase status
76	- [x] Phase 0 — Tooling setup (skills installed, cleaned up)
77	- [x] Phase 1 — Landing page visual direction (locked 2026-09-12)
78	- [x] Phase 2 — Hero cover assets generated, normalised and exported (2026-09-12)
79	- [ ] Phase 3 — Landing page copy/content (near-zero copy, per user)
80	- [ ] Phase 4 — Section-by-section build spec
81	- [~] Phase 5 — Scroll animation. Opening mechanic **built and published** as `hero-prototype.html` (artifact: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/5851f89e-44d6-4995-907a-19402028b896). Awaiting sign-off on the roundel question. Live aayat overlay still to do.
82	
83	## Open questions (asked 2026-09-12) — answered
84	1. Hero mood/atmosphere — **both light and dark mode** (not a single mood); use `ui-ux-pro-max` for the actual palette rather than guessing.
85	2. How literal the "opening" moment should look — **realistic**, but explicitly not a symmetrical center-split (reads as AI-generated). Also: 3-4 different aayat should cycle in as the user scrolls.
86	3. Setting/background around the Quran — **atmospheric elements only** (floating dust/light particles, no literal setting).
87	4. Landing page copy density — **almost none**, visual carries everything.
88	
89	## Page structure (locked 2026-09-12)
90	
91	The whole page, in scroll order. Nothing else gets added without a reason.
92	
93	1. **Rest** — book closed, centred, quiet wordmark.
94	2. **Opening** — scroll swings the cover open, the free edge on the left sweeping rightward, pivoting on the right-hand spine. The book translates left as it goes so it stays centred. Nothing else happens during this; the opening is the entire event.
95	3. **Fully open** — the book settles open, pages visible. No text yet.
96	4. **Aayat** — only now do the verses appear, 3-4 of them, cycling on the open pages as scrolling continues.
97	5. **Close** — one short line saying what the site is, one restrained entry point.
98	
99	**Deliberately excluded:** feature grids, testimonials, stat counters, newsletter signup, FAQ, link-farm footer. The user asked for "pure atmosphere"; the wordmark and closing line are the minimum needed for a visitor to know what they're looking at and how to enter. Everything beyond that is template furniture.
100	
101	## Opening animation — CSS, not video (decided 2026-09-13)
102	
103	**Veo is dropped for the opening.** A symmetric centre split is a geometric
104	transform, not paper physics — it is two `rotateY` transforms, so generating it as
105	video buys nothing and costs everything that went wrong in attempt 1.
106	
107	Built instead from two flat stills plus CSS:
108	
109	- `assets/hero/quran-dark.webp` — the closed cover, already approved
110	- an open-spread still (two blank cream pages) — **the one asset still to generate**
111	
112	The closed cover is drawn as two halves, left and right. Scroll drives each half
113	outward on `rotateY`, pivoting on its **outer** edge, revealing the spread beneath.
114	
115	Why this is strictly better than the video:
116	
117	| Problem in attempt 1 | Under CSS |
118	|---|---|
119	| Gemini watermark | Gone — nothing is generated as video |
120	| Camera drift / scale growth | Impossible — there is no camera |
121	| Direction reversal | Impossible — scroll position *is* the rotation angle |
122	| Ghost / dissolve morphing | Impossible — the asset never changes |
123	| Mirrored calligraphy on the inside face | We define the inside face ourselves |
124	| ~3 MB video + frame extraction | Two images, no decode step |
125	| Light/dark variants | Swap the image; the transform is identical |
126	
127	**Inside faces (locked 2026-09-13):** the reverse of each cover half is plain
128	endpaper — flat near-black, no roundel, no gold rule, no reversed script, nothing
129	showing through. The user called this out explicitly. In CSS this is a separate
130	back-face layer, not a flipped copy of the front.
131	
132	### The roundel conflict
133	
134	The gold roundel carrying القرآن الكريم sits dead centre, so a centre split cuts it
135	in half. Two ways out:
136	
137	1. **Fade the roundel and gold rules out over the first ~15% of the scroll, before
138	   the split begins** — the cover becomes a plain black field, then parts.
139	   **Recommended.** Nothing sacred is ever torn.
140	2. Let it split cleanly as a gatefold would. Geometrically clean, but it does divide
141	   the calligraphy down the middle.
142	
143	Going with (1) unless the user says otherwise — it is a one-line change either way.
144	
145	## Opening animation — superseded Veo approach (decided 2026-09-12)
146	
147	**Veo frame sequence**, generated **image-to-video** from `assets/hero/quran-dark.webp` as the starting frame — not text-to-video. This guarantees frame 1 is the approved hero asset, so there is no seam or colour mismatch between the static state and the animation.
148	
149	Non-negotiables in the generation: locked-off camera, unchanged lighting, flat identical background, book centred at constant scale, **blank cream pages with no text of any kind**, cover swinging **left to right**, and constant-speed motion with no easing (easing fights scroll-scrubbing).
150	
151	Frames get extracted and drawn to canvas on scroll. Real aayat are laid over the open pages as live text — never generated.
152	
153	**Audio:** Veo generates sound, and produced a door-creak effect on the first attempt. Irrelevant either way — we extract frames and discard the audio track entirely. A silent-clip instruction is included in the prompt only to stop the model shaping the motion around an imagined sound.
154	
155	**Sway (requested 2026-09-12):** the book should sway slightly around its vertical axis as it opens. This is built in **CSS, not Veo** — a small scroll-driven `rotateY` on the canvas element. Baking it into the video would violate the locked-off camera rule, make frames impossible to match to the static asset, and remove any ability to tune the amount. Keep the generated footage dead-on and flat; add dimensionality in code where it stays adjustable.
156	
157	### Attempt 1 rejected (2026-09-13)
158	
159	`videos/The_book_s_front_cover_swings.mp4` (1280×720, 10s) failed on six counts —
160	direction reverses at ~6.4s after a ghost/dissolve at ~5.5s, camera zooms and drifts
161	right, it opens past the cover to a middle spread, pages carry foxing stains, and a
162	Gemini sparkle watermark sits bottom-right throughout.
163	
164	**Diagnosed by extracting frames, not by eye** — see `videos/grab-frames.ps1`.
165	
166	**Strategy change:** pin **both** ends. Use Google Flow's *Frames to Video*
167	(first frame + last frame) rather than first-frame-only image-to-video, and shorten
168	the clip to 5–6s. A 10s unconstrained generation gives the model too much room to
169	drift; pinning only frame 1 is not enough to stop it. This adds a prerequisite —
170	an approved **end-frame still** (`quran-dark-open.webp`: same camera, same scale,
171	cover fully open to the right, one blank cream page), generated with Imagen under
172	the same flat-asset principle and normalised to the same canvas.
173	
174	Full failure table, corrected prompt, negative prompt, and the delivery checklist:
175	[videos/veo-prompt.md](videos/veo-prompt.md).
176	
177	**Tooling note:** system `ffmpeg` (`C:\ffmpeg-8.1.2-essentials_build\bin\`) is a
178	broken 533 KB install missing its DLLs — it exits 0 and silently does nothing.
179	Python is blocked from executing inside the Claude sandbox. `videos/grab-frames.ps1`
180	works around both with pure .NET WPF `MediaPlayer` scrubbing.
181	
182	## Picking this up on another machine
183	
184	`PLAN.md` is the handoff document — point a Claude session at this folder and it has full context. This is deliberate; an earlier session's planning files were lost when a scratch workspace was cleared.
185	
186	**Must transfer** (under 1 MB): `PLAN.md`, `design-system/quran-landing/MASTER.md`, `assets/hero/`.
187	**Don't bother** — re-creatable: `.agents/` + `.claude/` skills (~4 MB, re-run the installs below), and the `.jfif` originals (~3.7 MB, superseded by the normalised WebPs).
188	
189	```bash
190	npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill
191	```
192	Then inside a Claude Code session: `/plugin marketplace add nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill` and `/plugin install ui-ux-pro-max@ui-ux-pro-max-skill`.
193	
194	Python 3.12 + Pillow + numpy are only needed to re-run the asset normalisation scripts.
195	
196	## ⚠ Something on this machine stamps .jpg files (found 2026-09-13)
197	
198	**Do not save project assets as `.jpg` on this PC.** Something is rewriting JPEG
199	files and stamping `I am Sorry !!!!!` into the bottom-left corner.
200	
201	Evidence:
202	
203	- Four `.jpg` files written at ~00:36 were all silently rewritten at **00:49:08**
204	  with different file sizes and different hashes. Nothing in this session did that.
205	- Every one carried the same stamp at the same place — bbox `x 11..576, y 929..1053`
206	  on a 1920×1080 frame, identical across files with completely different content.
207	- The text is **dark**, so it is invisible on dark areas and only shows on light
208	  ones. It was spotted on the cream pages of `spread-dark.jpg`; it was equally
209	  present on `frame-first.jpg` and only found by boosting the levels 7×.
210	- `open-spread.jfif` and `quran-dark.webp` were **never touched**. The stamper
211	  appears to target `.jpg` only.
212	
213	**Workaround in use:** build frames straight from the untouched sources to **PNG**,
214	never landing on an intermediate `.jpg`. See `C:\Temp\qf\rebuild-png.ps1`.
215	
216	**Verify before every upload.** Boost the levels on the bottom-left corner and look —
217	a visual glance is not enough, because the stamp hides on dark ground. `corner.ps1`
218	flags it: a bbox starting left of x=382 (outside the book) means the file is stamped.
219	
220	The user should find out what is doing this. Until then, treat any `.jpg` written to
221	this project as suspect.
222	
223	## Hero assets (built 2026-09-12)
224	
225	| File | Purpose |
226	|------|---------|
227	| `assets/hero/quran-dark.webp` | Dark-mode cover, 2816×1536, 402 KB |
228	| `assets/hero/quran-light.webp` | Light-mode cover, 2816×1536, 183 KB |
229	| `assets/hero/quran-dark@1x.webp` | Half-size, 1408×768 |
230	| `assets/hero/quran-light@1x.webp` | Half-size, 1408×768 |
231	
232	### Animation assets (2026-09-13) — tight crops, no padding
233	
234	The padded assets above are hero *display* stills. The split animation needs the
235	book with **no surrounding background**, or the rotating halves would carry
236	background-coloured rectangles with them.
237	
238	| File | Size | Purpose |
239	|------|------|---------|
240	| `assets/hero/cover-dark.jpg` | 907×1349, 493 KB | Closed cover, tight crop. Split down the middle into two leaves. |
241	| `assets/hero/spread-dark.jpg` | 1814×1349, 167 KB | Open spread, tight crop. Each page exactly 907 = cover width. |
242	| `assets/hero/open-spread.jfif` | 2752×1536 | Imagen original, kept |
243	| `assets/hero/frame-first.jpg` | 1920×1080, 287 KB | **Start frame for generation.** Closed cover, spine on the exact centre (x=960). |
244	| `assets/hero/frame-last.jpg` | 1920×1080, 117 KB | **End frame for generation.** Open spread, fold on the exact centre (x=960). |
245	
246	The two generation frames are **composed, not generated** — both are built from the
247	approved stills by `C:\Temp\qf\frames.ps1` on a 1920×1080 near-black canvas, book
248	height 860 at y=110, cover at x 382..960 and spread at x 382..1538. Because the
249	closed cover occupies exactly where the first page will be, and the spine and fold
250	both land on x=960, the model has no room to reposition, rescale or drift.
251	
252	Rebuild them by re-running `crop.ps1` → `tojpg.ps1` → `frames.ps1`.
253	
254	Measured before cropping — the spread came back genuinely clean: fold 2px off
255	canvas centre, pages 956/956 with **0px** difference, background flat at lum 27
256	across the whole field with no baked halo, pages unmarked.
257	
258	The spread was 5.5% wider per page than the cover, so it was scaled non-uniformly
259	(0.948 × 0.984) to make each page exactly 907×1349. On blank cream paper that
260	differential is invisible, and it makes cover and pages align exactly.
261	
262	Convert both to WebP before shipping — these are JPEGs only because nothing on this
263	machine can encode WebP.
264	
265	Originals kept as `dark quran image.jfif` / `light quran image.jfif`.
266	
267	The two generations did not match as delivered — dark book measured 906×1350, light 840×1211, on different canvases (2816 vs 2752 wide), with the light one slightly off-centre. Both were rescaled to a common 1350px book height and recentred on an identical 2816×1536 canvas, so a theme toggle swaps them with no visible jump. Regenerate-and-hope was avoided deliberately; if either asset is ever regenerated, re-run the same normalisation.
268	
269	Note: the dark generation's background carries a faint gradient rather than being perfectly flat. Its base tone reads `rgb(27,27,27)` ≈ `#1B1B1B`, near-identical to the locked `#1C1917` ground, so it composites cleanly regardless.
270	
271	## Decisions log
272	- 2026-09-12 — Scope locked to landing page only.
273	- 2026-09-12 — Stack locked to plain HTML/CSS/JS.
274	- 2026-09-12 — Hero mechanic locked: scroll-scrubbed Quran-opening animation.
275	- 2026-09-12 — Hero image will be AI-generated (not real photography) — user's call, since no legible verse text is required in this shot.
276	- 2026-09-12 — Installed Python 3.12 (via winget) so `ui-ux-pro-max`'s search tool could actually run instead of guessing at its data.
277	- 2026-09-12 — Palette/typography/motion spec locked via `ui-ux-pro-max`, dark-mode variant hand-derived per its own contrast rule. Full detail in [design-system/quran-landing/MASTER.md](design-system/quran-landing/MASTER.md).
278	- 2026-09-12 — User has Google Pro (Imagen/Veo via Gemini) — generation prompts are being written for that toolset.
279	- 2026-09-13 — Veo attempt 1 rejected. Switching to first-frame + last-frame interpolation and a 5–6s clip, which requires generating an approved open-book end-frame still first.
280	- 2026-09-13 — Video QA is done by extracting frames and checking them against the locked non-negotiables, not by watching playback. Script committed at `videos/grab-frames.ps1`.
281	- 2026-09-13 — Centre-split tried at user's request, built as `hero-prototype.html`, and **rejected on sight as physically fake**. The "no centre split" rule is reinstated and is now settled — it has been tested, not just asserted. Cover pivots on the right-hand spine.
282	- 2026-09-13 — **Veo reinstated for the opening.** A realistic cover swing involves paper flex, page-block settling and a moving hinge — genuinely video's job, unlike the centre split which was pure geometry.
283	- 2026-09-13 — Generation frames the **spine at the exact centre**; recentring is a scroll-driven `translateX` in CSS. Keeps the camera locked in the generation and the composition tunable in code.
284	- 2026-09-13 — Inside of the front cover is plain cream endpaper — never a mirrored copy of the front calligraphy. User called this out directly.
