# Quran Landing Page — Project Plan

## Goal
A $10,000-quality landing page for a Quran website — a pure visual "hook," not the full site. Everything beyond the landing page is out of scope until this phase is locked and built.

## Why this approach (history)
- **Attempt 1:** Full site research (page/media structure), hardcoded directly in Opus. Effort got diluted across too much scope at once — came out wrong.
- **Attempt 2:** Landing-page-only, user-supplied Quran images. Turned into one crammed single-page app with no real design system behind it — looked cheap, not "like a Claude website."
- **Attempt 3 (this plan):** Claude plans phase-by-phase here first. Each phase is locked before the next starts. User pastes each locked phase into Opus ("ultracode" = Claude run at max effort, not a separate tool) to hardcode.

## Stack
Plain HTML/CSS/JS. No build tools, no framework — so each phase can be pasted in and seen working immediately.

## Hero concept
Scroll-scrubbed animation: as the user scrolls, the Quran visually opens (cover lifts / pages part) — Apple product-page style, scroll position drives playback, not autoplay.
- Static hero image generated by AI first (this phase).
- Video/animation frames generated in a later phase — **hold off on video prompts until user confirms that phase has started.**
- User has Google Pro (Imagen/Veo via Gemini) — generation prompts should target that toolset.

## Hard constraint: AI + Arabic text
AI image/video generators reliably mangle Arabic script. Any visual needing legible Quranic verse text must use real photography/calligraphy instead. AI generation is fine for the Quran object itself and for atmospheric elements (light, dust, geometric motion, texture) as long as no readable verse text is required in the render.

## Design direction
Elegant, simple, built for a lasting/memorable impression — not maximalist or feature-crowded. Must support **both light and dark mode properly** (dark is not just an inverted light mode).

Full palette, typography, spacing, motion spec, and pre-delivery checklist: [design-system/quran-landing/MASTER.md](design-system/quran-landing/MASTER.md) — generated + persisted via the `ui-ux-pro-max` skill (real database query, not invented), with a hand-derived dark-mode palette layered on top since the tool only returns one fixed palette per query.

- **Palette:** Primary near-black `#1C1917`, background `#FAFAF9`, gold accent `#A16207` (light) / `#D4AF37` (dark) — "Premium black + gold."
- **Typography:** Bodoni Moda (headings) + Jost (body) — luxury/minimalist/refined pairing.
- **Hero opening mechanic (RESTORED 2026-09-13):** the cover lifts from its free edge and swings on the spine. It must NOT split symmetrically from the centre.

  **This rule was reversed and then reinstated the same day.** A centre split was tried at the user's request, built, and rejected on sight: *"how can a book magically open from the center when its spine is on the right."* There is no hinge at the centre of a bound book, so the motion reads as fake no matter how cleanly it is executed. Treat this rule as settled and do not reopen it — the prototype that proved it is at `hero-prototype.html`.

- **The book must translate as it opens.** Closed, the book occupies width W. The cover pivots on the right-hand spine and swings rightward, so when open the pair spans 2W — the growth is entirely to the **right**. Left unhandled, the book slides off-centre as it opens.

  **Fix — put the spine at the exact centre of the generated frame, and do the recentring in CSS.** The generation keeps a dead-locked camera (no pan, no zoom, nothing for the model to drift); the element is then translated on scroll from `+W/2` (closed book reads centred) to `0` (open spread reads centred). This is the "move it" the user asked for, kept in code where it stays tunable instead of baked into footage.

- **Inside of the front cover = plain cream endpaper.** Never a mirrored or reversed copy of the front calligraphy, never the roundel showing through. With the inside cream, the open state reads as a proper two-page spread.
- **Hero pose (corrected 2026-09-12):** book stands upright, front cover facing the camera nearly head-on — not lying flat / not a three-quarter table-top shot. Spine is a vertical edge on the right side of frame, page edge on the left.
- **Opening direction (corrected 2026-09-12 — earlier entries had this backwards):** the cover swings **left to right**. The spine is on the right, so the *free* edge is on the left; it lifts and sweeps rightward, pivoting on the right-hand spine. This is the mirror of a Western book. Do not confuse it with Arabic *reading* direction, which is right-to-left — the text flows RTL while the physical page motion goes LTR. Conflating the two is what produced the earlier error.
- **Working order:** perfecting the dark-mode hero image alone first; light-mode variant comes after dark is locked.

### Asset principle (locked 2026-09-12) — applies to every generated image and video
Generate **clean flat assets, not finished photographs.** No baked-in tilt, perspective, directional lighting, cast shadows, vignette, glow, or particles. Straight-on orthographic front view, evenly lit corner to corner, flat solid background, tight crop.

**Why:** baked-in lighting and perspective can't be re-themed between light and dark mode, and a tilted source fights the scroll-open animation. Glow, shadows, atmospheric particles, and depth are built in CSS/canvas at implementation time — animatable, themeable, and far lighter than shipping two moody photographs. The generated asset is the book; the hero section is composed around it in code.

**Flat means flat:** no page edges visible on the left, no spine edge visible on the right, no book thickness at all — only the rectangular cover face. If either edge is visible, there is still rotation in the image.

**Cover colourway (locked):** near-black / deep espresso leather with antique gold tooling — not mid-brown. Chosen so the asset sits natively on the `#1C1917` dark ground with `#D4AF37` gold, per the design system.

**Cover design language (locked 2026-09-12, from user reference):** restrained and minimal, not densely ornate. Black field with subtle low-relief tone-on-tone texture, one thin gold double-rule border inset from the edges, single small gold roundel centred. Sparing gold. The earlier heavily-tooled arabesque direction is rejected as too busy.

**Calligraphy (revised 2026-09-12):** the centre roundel carries القرآن الكريم, generated directly in the image. This short phrase appears on a huge number of real covers and renders acceptably; the earlier blanket "never generate Arabic" rule was too strict for it. Verify the glyphs by eye before shipping — subtle malformation is the failure mode.

Longer or less common Arabic — the scrolling aayat above all — still must be live text, never generated artwork.

**Orientation — two separate things, state both every time:**
- **Canvas:** landscape 16:9 (approved black asset is 2816×1536). Never a portrait canvas.
- **Book:** portrait, roughly 2:3, centred in that landscape canvas with empty background either side, whole and uncropped.

Conflating these produced a mismatched pair once already — the white variant came back as a tight portrait crop (1846×2304).

**Asset pair (locked 2026-09-12):** dark-mode cover approved. The light-mode cover is the same asset in ivory-white with gold — identical composition, proportions, border, roundel placement and framing, colourway only. Not a horizontal flip; spine side stays consistent. The two must stay pixel-compatible so toggling theme swaps the image without shifting layout.

**Output size:** roughly 1200–1600px tall is plenty for a hero asset; convert to WebP for the build (the design system checklist requires WebP/AVIF). No need for huge multi-MB generations.
- **Aayat on scroll:** 3-4 different verses should appear/cycle as the user scrolls the hero. This text must be real type (HTML/CSS text or a proper Arabic font), never baked into the AI-generated image or video — same reason AI can't render legible Arabic script reliably. The static hero image and generated video stay text-free; verse overlays are a separate live-text layer built in Phase 5.
- The design system's suggested page "Pattern" (multi-chapter problem/journey/solution) does not fit this brief — only its motion, accessibility, and anti-pattern rules apply, not its section structure.

## Tooling installed (this folder)
- `design-taste-frontend`, `full-output-enforcement`, `high-end-visual-design`, `image-to-code`, `imagegen-frontend-web`, `minimalist-ui` — from Leonxlnx/taste-skill
- `ui-ux-pro-max` — design-system skill (palettes, font pairings, UX rules)
- `web-design-guidelines` — audit skill, to be used once a draft exists to check

## Phase status
- [x] Phase 0 — Tooling setup (skills installed, cleaned up)
- [x] Phase 1 — Landing page visual direction (locked 2026-09-12)
- [x] Phase 2 — Hero cover assets generated, normalised and exported (2026-09-12)
- [ ] Phase 3 — Landing page copy/content (near-zero copy, per user)
- [ ] Phase 4 — Section-by-section build spec
- [~] Phase 5 — Scroll animation. Opening mechanic **built and published** as `hero-prototype.html` (artifact: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/5851f89e-44d6-4995-907a-19402028b896). Awaiting sign-off on the roundel question. Live aayat overlay still to do.

## Open questions (asked 2026-09-12) — answered
1. Hero mood/atmosphere — **both light and dark mode** (not a single mood); use `ui-ux-pro-max` for the actual palette rather than guessing.
2. How literal the "opening" moment should look — **realistic**, but explicitly not a symmetrical center-split (reads as AI-generated). Also: 3-4 different aayat should cycle in as the user scrolls.
3. Setting/background around the Quran — **atmospheric elements only** (floating dust/light particles, no literal setting).
4. Landing page copy density — **almost none**, visual carries everything.

## Page structure (locked 2026-09-12)

The whole page, in scroll order. Nothing else gets added without a reason.

1. **Rest** — book closed, centred, quiet wordmark.
2. **Opening** — scroll swings the cover open, the free edge on the left sweeping rightward, pivoting on the right-hand spine. The book translates left as it goes so it stays centred. Nothing else happens during this; the opening is the entire event.
3. **Fully open** — the book settles open, pages visible. No text yet.
4. **Aayat** — only now do the verses appear, 3-4 of them, cycling on the open pages as scrolling continues.
5. **Close** — one short line saying what the site is, one restrained entry point.

**Deliberately excluded:** feature grids, testimonials, stat counters, newsletter signup, FAQ, link-farm footer. The user asked for "pure atmosphere"; the wordmark and closing line are the minimum needed for a visitor to know what they're looking at and how to enter. Everything beyond that is template furniture.

## Opening animation — CSS, not video (decided 2026-09-13)

**Veo is dropped for the opening.** A symmetric centre split is a geometric
transform, not paper physics — it is two `rotateY` transforms, so generating it as
video buys nothing and costs everything that went wrong in attempt 1.

Built instead from two flat stills plus CSS:

- `assets/hero/quran-dark.webp` — the closed cover, already approved
- an open-spread still (two blank cream pages) — **the one asset still to generate**

The closed cover is drawn as two halves, left and right. Scroll drives each half
outward on `rotateY`, pivoting on its **outer** edge, revealing the spread beneath.

Why this is strictly better than the video:

| Problem in attempt 1 | Under CSS |
|---|---|
| Gemini watermark | Gone — nothing is generated as video |
| Camera drift / scale growth | Impossible — there is no camera |
| Direction reversal | Impossible — scroll position *is* the rotation angle |
| Ghost / dissolve morphing | Impossible — the asset never changes |
| Mirrored calligraphy on the inside face | We define the inside face ourselves |
| ~3 MB video + frame extraction | Two images, no decode step |
| Light/dark variants | Swap the image; the transform is identical |

**Inside faces (locked 2026-09-13):** the reverse of each cover half is plain
endpaper — flat near-black, no roundel, no gold rule, no reversed script, nothing
showing through. The user called this out explicitly. In CSS this is a separate
back-face layer, not a flipped copy of the front.

### The roundel conflict

The gold roundel carrying القرآن الكريم sits dead centre, so a centre split cuts it
in half. Two ways out:

1. **Fade the roundel and gold rules out over the first ~15% of the scroll, before
   the split begins** — the cover becomes a plain black field, then parts.
   **Recommended.** Nothing sacred is ever torn.
2. Let it split cleanly as a gatefold would. Geometrically clean, but it does divide
   the calligraphy down the middle.

Going with (1) unless the user says otherwise — it is a one-line change either way.

## Opening animation — superseded Veo approach (decided 2026-09-12)

**Veo frame sequence**, generated **image-to-video** from `assets/hero/quran-dark.webp` as the starting frame — not text-to-video. This guarantees frame 1 is the approved hero asset, so there is no seam or colour mismatch between the static state and the animation.

Non-negotiables in the generation: locked-off camera, unchanged lighting, flat identical background, book centred at constant scale, **blank cream pages with no text of any kind**, cover swinging **left to right**, and constant-speed motion with no easing (easing fights scroll-scrubbing).

Frames get extracted and drawn to canvas on scroll. Real aayat are laid over the open pages as live text — never generated.

**Audio:** Veo generates sound, and produced a door-creak effect on the first attempt. Irrelevant either way — we extract frames and discard the audio track entirely. A silent-clip instruction is included in the prompt only to stop the model shaping the motion around an imagined sound.

**Sway (requested 2026-09-12):** the book should sway slightly around its vertical axis as it opens. This is built in **CSS, not Veo** — a small scroll-driven `rotateY` on the canvas element. Baking it into the video would violate the locked-off camera rule, make frames impossible to match to the static asset, and remove any ability to tune the amount. Keep the generated footage dead-on and flat; add dimensionality in code where it stays adjustable.

### Attempt 1 rejected (2026-09-13)

`videos/The_book_s_front_cover_swings.mp4` (1280×720, 10s) failed on six counts —
direction reverses at ~6.4s after a ghost/dissolve at ~5.5s, camera zooms and drifts
right, it opens past the cover to a middle spread, pages carry foxing stains, and a
Gemini sparkle watermark sits bottom-right throughout.

**Diagnosed by extracting frames, not by eye** — see `videos/grab-frames.ps1`.

**Strategy change:** pin **both** ends. Use Google Flow's *Frames to Video*
(first frame + last frame) rather than first-frame-only image-to-video, and shorten
the clip to 5–6s. A 10s unconstrained generation gives the model too much room to
drift; pinning only frame 1 is not enough to stop it. This adds a prerequisite —
an approved **end-frame still** (`quran-dark-open.webp`: same camera, same scale,
cover fully open to the right, one blank cream page), generated with Imagen under
the same flat-asset principle and normalised to the same canvas.

Full failure table, corrected prompt, negative prompt, and the delivery checklist:
[videos/veo-prompt.md](videos/veo-prompt.md).

**Tooling note:** system `ffmpeg` (`C:\ffmpeg-8.1.2-essentials_build\bin\`) is a
broken 533 KB install missing its DLLs — it exits 0 and silently does nothing.
Python is blocked from executing inside the Claude sandbox. `videos/grab-frames.ps1`
works around both with pure .NET WPF `MediaPlayer` scrubbing.

## Picking this up on another machine

`PLAN.md` is the handoff document — point a Claude session at this folder and it has full context. This is deliberate; an earlier session's planning files were lost when a scratch workspace was cleared.

**Must transfer** (under 1 MB): `PLAN.md`, `design-system/quran-landing/MASTER.md`, `assets/hero/`.
**Don't bother** — re-creatable: `.agents/` + `.claude/` skills (~4 MB, re-run the installs below), and the `.jfif` originals (~3.7 MB, superseded by the normalised WebPs).

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill
```
Then inside a Claude Code session: `/plugin marketplace add nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill` and `/plugin install ui-ux-pro-max@ui-ux-pro-max-skill`.

Python 3.12 + Pillow + numpy are only needed to re-run the asset normalisation scripts.

## ⚠ Something on this machine stamps .jpg files (found 2026-09-13)

**Do not save project assets as `.jpg` on this PC.** Something is rewriting JPEG
files and stamping `I am Sorry !!!!!` into the bottom-left corner.

Evidence:

- Four `.jpg` files written at ~00:36 were all silently rewritten at **00:49:08**
  with different file sizes and different hashes. Nothing in this session did that.
- Every one carried the same stamp at the same place — bbox `x 11..576, y 929..1053`
  on a 1920×1080 frame, identical across files with completely different content.
- The text is **dark**, so it is invisible on dark areas and only shows on light
  ones. It was spotted on the cream pages of `spread-dark.jpg`; it was equally
  present on `frame-first.jpg` and only found by boosting the levels 7×.
- `open-spread.jfif` and `quran-dark.webp` were **never touched**. The stamper
  appears to target `.jpg` only.

**Workaround in use:** build frames straight from the untouched sources to **PNG**,
never landing on an intermediate `.jpg`. See `C:\Temp\qf\rebuild-png.ps1`.

**Verify before every upload.** Boost the levels on the bottom-left corner and look —
a visual glance is not enough, because the stamp hides on dark ground. `corner.ps1`
flags it: a bbox starting left of x=382 (outside the book) means the file is stamped.

The user should find out what is doing this. Until then, treat any `.jpg` written to
this project as suspect.

## Hero assets (built 2026-09-12)

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `assets/hero/quran-dark.webp` | Dark-mode cover, 2816×1536, 402 KB |
| `assets/hero/quran-light.webp` | Light-mode cover, 2816×1536, 183 KB |
| `assets/hero/quran-dark@1x.webp` | Half-size, 1408×768 |
| `assets/hero/quran-light@1x.webp` | Half-size, 1408×768 |

### Animation assets (2026-09-13) — tight crops, no padding

The padded assets above are hero *display* stills. The split animation needs the
book with **no surrounding background**, or the rotating halves would carry
background-coloured rectangles with them.

| File | Size | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `assets/hero/cover-dark.jpg` | 907×1349, 493 KB | Closed cover, tight crop. Split down the middle into two leaves. |
| `assets/hero/spread-dark.jpg` | 1814×1349, 167 KB | Open spread, tight crop. Each page exactly 907 = cover width. |
| `assets/hero/open-spread.jfif` | 2752×1536 | Imagen original, kept |
| `assets/hero/frame-first.jpg` | 1920×1080, 287 KB | **Start frame for generation.** Closed cover, spine on the exact centre (x=960). |
| `assets/hero/frame-last.jpg` | 1920×1080, 117 KB | **End frame for generation.** Open spread, fold on the exact centre (x=960). |

The two generation frames are **composed, not generated** — both are built from the
approved stills by `C:\Temp\qf\frames.ps1` on a 1920×1080 near-black canvas, book
height 860 at y=110, cover at x 382..960 and spread at x 382..1538. Because the
closed cover occupies exactly where the first page will be, and the spine and fold
both land on x=960, the model has no room to reposition, rescale or drift.

Rebuild them by re-running `crop.ps1` → `tojpg.ps1` → `frames.ps1`.

Measured before cropping — the spread came back genuinely clean: fold 2px off
canvas centre, pages 956/956 with **0px** difference, background flat at lum 27
across the whole field with no baked halo, pages unmarked.

The spread was 5.5% wider per page than the cover, so it was scaled non-uniformly
(0.948 × 0.984) to make each page exactly 907×1349. On blank cream paper that
differential is invisible, and it makes cover and pages align exactly.

Convert both to WebP before shipping — these are JPEGs only because nothing on this
machine can encode WebP.

Originals kept as `dark quran image.jfif` / `light quran image.jfif`.

The two generations did not match as delivered — dark book measured 906×1350, light 840×1211, on different canvases (2816 vs 2752 wide), with the light one slightly off-centre. Both were rescaled to a common 1350px book height and recentred on an identical 2816×1536 canvas, so a theme toggle swaps them with no visible jump. Regenerate-and-hope was avoided deliberately; if either asset is ever regenerated, re-run the same normalisation.

Note: the dark generation's background carries a faint gradient rather than being perfectly flat. Its base tone reads `rgb(27,27,27)` ≈ `#1B1B1B`, near-identical to the locked `#1C1917` ground, so it composites cleanly regardless.

## Decisions log
- 2026-09-12 — Scope locked to landing page only.
- 2026-09-12 — Stack locked to plain HTML/CSS/JS.
- 2026-09-12 — Hero mechanic locked: scroll-scrubbed Quran-opening animation.
- 2026-09-12 — Hero image will be AI-generated (not real photography) — user's call, since no legible verse text is required in this shot.
- 2026-09-12 — Installed Python 3.12 (via winget) so `ui-ux-pro-max`'s search tool could actually run instead of guessing at its data.
- 2026-09-12 — Palette/typography/motion spec locked via `ui-ux-pro-max`, dark-mode variant hand-derived per its own contrast rule. Full detail in [design-system/quran-landing/MASTER.md](design-system/quran-landing/MASTER.md).
- 2026-09-12 — User has Google Pro (Imagen/Veo via Gemini) — generation prompts are being written for that toolset.
- 2026-09-13 — Veo attempt 1 rejected. Switching to first-frame + last-frame interpolation and a 5–6s clip, which requires generating an approved open-book end-frame still first.
- 2026-09-13 — Video QA is done by extracting frames and checking them against the locked non-negotiables, not by watching playback. Script committed at `videos/grab-frames.ps1`.
- 2026-09-13 — Centre-split tried at user's request, built as `hero-prototype.html`, and **rejected on sight as physically fake**. The "no centre split" rule is reinstated and is now settled — it has been tested, not just asserted. Cover pivots on the right-hand spine.
- 2026-09-13 — **Veo reinstated for the opening.** A realistic cover swing involves paper flex, page-block settling and a moving hinge — genuinely video's job, unlike the centre split which was pure geometry.
- 2026-09-13 — Generation frames the **spine at the exact centre**; recentring is a scroll-driven `translateX` in CSS. Keeps the camera locked in the generation and the composition tunable in code.
- 2026-09-13 — Inside of the front cover is plain cream endpaper — never a mirrored copy of the front calligraphy. User called this out directly.

8	
9	- `color-contrast` - Minimum 4.5:1 ratio for normal text (large text 3:1); Material Design
10	- `focus-states` - Visible focus rings on interactive elements (2–4px; Apple HIG, MD)
11	- `alt-text` - Descriptive alt text for meaningful images
12	- `aria-labels` - aria-label for icon-only buttons; accessibilityLabel in native (Apple HIG)
13	- `icon-context` - Semantics depend on use: decorative icons beside visible text are hidden from the accessibility tree; meaningful icons need a text alternative; icon controls need an accessible name and applicable state
14	- `keyboard-nav` - Tab order matches visual order; full keyboard support (Apple HIG)
15	- `form-labels` - Use label with for attribute
16	- `skip-links` - Skip to main content for keyboard users
17	- `heading-hierarchy` - Sequential h1→h6, no level skip
18	- `color-not-only` - Don't convey info by color alone (add icon/text)
19	- `dynamic-type` - Support system text scaling; avoid truncation as text grows (Apple Dynamic Type, MD)
20	- `reduced-motion` - Respect prefers-reduced-motion; reduce/disable animations when requested (Apple Reduced Motion API, MD)
21	- `voiceover-sr` - Meaningful accessibilityLabel/accessibilityHint; logical reading order for VoiceOver/screen readers (Apple HIG, MD)
22	- `escape-routes` - Provide cancel/back in modals and multi-step flows (Apple HIG)
23	- `keyboard-shortcuts` - Preserve system and a11y shortcuts; offer keyboard alternatives for drag-and-drop (Apple HIG)
24	- `focus-not-obscured` - Sticky UI, overlays, and banners must not hide the keyboard-focused control (WCAG 2.2 AA)
25	- `focus-not-obscured-enhanced` - Keep the entire focused component visible (WCAG 2.2 AAA)
26	- `focus-appearance` - Verify focus indicator area and 3:1 state contrast; visible focus alone is not enough (WCAG 2.2 AAA)
27	- `dragging-alternative` - Every author-controlled drag action needs a single-pointer and keyboard alternative (WCAG 2.2 AA)
28	- `web-target-size` - Web pointer targets need 24×24 CSS px or a documented exception; do not substitute native units (WCAG 2.2 AA)
29	- `consistent-help` - Repeated help mechanisms stay in the same relative order across a page set (WCAG 2.2 A)
30	- `redundant-entry` - Reuse information already supplied in the same process unless re-entry is essential (WCAG 2.2 A)
31	- `accessible-authentication` - Allow password managers and paste; provide a non-cognitive authentication path (WCAG 2.2 Minimum, AA). The Enhanced AAA criterion is not represented in the dataset
32	- `auto-rotation-controls` - Carousels and moving content need pause/stop controls and must stop on focus or reduced motion (WAI)
33	- `contextual-live-badge-updates` - Announce a changed count/status as a complete contextual phrase without moving focus; use one appropriate live/status region and atomic updates only when needed
34	
35	### 2. Touch & Interaction (CRITICAL)
36	
37	- `touch-target-size` - Min 44×44pt (Apple) / 48×48dp (Material); extend hit area beyond visual bounds if needed
38	- `touch-spacing` - Minimum 8px/8dp gap between touch targets (Apple HIG, MD)
39	- `hover-vs-tap` - Use click/tap for primary interactions; don't rely on hover alone
40	- `loading-buttons` - Disable button during async operations; show spinner or progress
41	- `error-feedback` - Clear error messages near problem
42	- `cursor-pointer` - Add cursor-pointer to clickable elements (Web)
43	- `gesture-conflicts` - Avoid horizontal swipe on main content; prefer vertical scroll
44	- `tap-delay` - Use touch-action: manipulation to reduce 300ms delay (Web)
45	- `standard-gestures` - Use platform standard gestures consistently; don't redefine (e.g. swipe-back, pinch-zoom) (Apple HIG)
46	- `system-gestures` - Don't block system gestures (Control Center, back swipe, etc.) (Apple HIG)
47	- `press-feedback` - Visual feedback on press (ripple/highlight; MD state layers)
48	- `haptic-feedback` - Use haptic for confirmations and important actions; avoid overuse (Apple HIG)
49	- `gesture-alternative` - Don't rely on gesture-only interactions; always provide visible controls for critical actions
50	- `safe-area-awareness` - Keep primary touch targets away from notch, Dynamic Island, gesture bar and screen edges
51	- `no-precision-required` - Avoid requiring pixel-perfect taps on small icons or thin edges
52	- `swipe-clarity` - Swipe actions must show clear affordance or hint (chevron, label, tutorial)
53	- `drag-threshold` - Use a movement threshold before starting drag to avoid accidental drags
54	
55	### 3. Performance (HIGH)
56	
57	- `image-optimization` - Use WebP/AVIF, responsive images (srcset/sizes), lazy load non-critical assets
58	- `image-dimension` - Declare width/height or use aspect-ratio to prevent layout shift (Core Web Vitals: CLS)
59	- `font-loading` - Use font-display: swap/optional to avoid invisible text (FOIT); reserve space to reduce layout shift (MD)
60	- `font-preload` - Preload only critical fonts; avoid overusing preload on every variant
61	- `critical-css` - Prioritize above-the-fold CSS (inline critical CSS or early-loaded stylesheet)
62	- `lazy-loading` - Lazy load non-hero components via dynamic import / route-level splitting
63	- `bundle-splitting` - Split code by route/feature (React Suspense / Next.js dynamic) to reduce initial load and TTI
64	- `third-party-scripts` - Load third-party scripts async/defer; audit and remove unnecessary ones (MD)
65	- `reduce-reflows` - Avoid frequent layout reads/writes; batch DOM reads then writes
66	- `content-jumping` - Reserve space for async content to avoid layout jumps (Core Web Vitals: CLS)
67	- `lazy-load-below-fold` - Use loading="lazy" for below-the-fold images and heavy media
68	- `virtualize-lists` - Virtualize lists with 50+ items to improve memory efficiency and scroll performance
69	- `main-thread-budget` - Keep per-frame work under ~16ms for 60fps; move heavy tasks off main thread (HIG, MD)
70	- `progressive-loading` - Use skeleton screens / shimmer instead of long blocking spinners for >1s operations (Apple HIG)
71	- `input-latency` - Keep input latency under ~100ms for taps/scrolls (Material responsiveness standard)
72	- `tap-feedback-speed` - Provide visual feedback within 100ms of tap (Apple HIG)
73	- `debounce-throttle` - Use debounce/throttle for high-frequency events (scroll, resize, input)
74	- `offline-support` - Provide offline state messaging and basic fallback (PWA / mobile)
75	- `network-fallback` - Offer degraded modes for slow networks (lower-res images, fewer animations)
76	
77	### 4. Style Selection (HIGH)
78	
79	- `style-match` - Match style to product type (use `--design-system` for recommendations)
80	- `consistency` - Use same style across all pages
81	- `no-emoji-icons` - Use SVG icons (Heroicons, Lucide), not emojis
82	- `color-palette-from-product` - Choose palette from product/industry (search `--domain color`)
83	- `effects-match-style` - Shadows, blur, radius aligned with chosen style (glass / flat / clay etc.)
84	- `platform-adaptive` - Respect platform idioms (iOS HIG vs Material): navigation, controls, typography, motion
85	- `state-clarity` - Make hover/pressed/disabled states visually distinct while staying on-style (Material state layers)
86	- `elevation-consistent` - Use a consistent elevation/shadow scale for cards, sheets, modals; avoid random shadow values
87	- `dark-mode-pairing` - Design light/dark variants together to keep brand, contrast, and style consistent
88	- `icon-style-consistent` - Use one icon set/visual language (stroke width, corner radius) across the product
89	- `system-controls` - Prefer native/system controls over fully custom ones; only customize when branding requires it (Apple HIG)
90	- `blur-purpose` - Use blur to indicate background dismissal (modals, sheets), not as decoration (Apple HIG)
91	- `primary-action` - Each screen should have only one primary CTA; secondary actions visually subordinate (Apple HIG)
92	
93	### 5. Layout & Responsive (HIGH)
94	
95	- `viewport-meta` - width=device-width initial-scale=1 (never disable zoom)
96	- `mobile-first` - Design mobile-first, then scale up to tablet and desktop
97	- `breakpoint-consistency` - Use systematic breakpoints (e.g. 375 / 768 / 1024 / 1440)
98	- `readable-font-size` - Minimum 16px body text on mobile (avoids iOS auto-zoom)
99	- `line-length-control` - Mobile 35–60 chars per line; desktop 60–75 chars
100	- `horizontal-scroll` - No horizontal scroll on mobile; ensure content fits viewport width
101	- `spacing-scale` - Use 4pt/8dp incremental spacing system (Material Design)
102	- `touch-density` - Keep component spacing comfortable for touch: not cramped, not causing mis-taps
103	- `container-width` - Consistent max-width on desktop (max-w-6xl / 7xl)
104	- `z-index-management` - Define layered z-index scale (e.g. 0 / 10 / 20 / 40 / 100 / 1000)
105	- `fixed-element-offset` - Fixed navbar/bottom bar must reserve safe padding for underlying content
106	- `scroll-behavior` - Avoid nested scroll regions that interfere with the main scroll experience
107	- `viewport-units` - Prefer min-h-dvh over 100vh on mobile
108	- `orientation-support` - Keep layout readable and operable in landscape mode
109	- `content-priority` - Show core content first on mobile; fold or hide secondary content
110	- `visual-hierarchy` - Establish hierarchy via size, spacing, contrast — not color alone
111	- `compact-label-overflow` - Choose badge, status tag, filter chip, or removable value from its semantics; keep essential labels available and disclose unavoidable truncation to pointer and keyboard users
112	- `chip-collection-reflow` - Wrap the collection before shrinking labels; make a `+n` overflow summary an operable disclosure instead of hiding values
113	
114	### 6. Typography & Color (MEDIUM)
115	
116	- `line-height` - Use 1.5-1.75 for body text
117	- `line-length` - Limit to 65-75 characters per line
118	- `font-pairing` - Match heading/body font personalities
119	- `font-scale` - Consistent type scale (e.g. 12 14 16 18 24 32)
120	- `contrast-readability` - Darker text on light backgrounds (e.g. slate-900 on white)
121	- `text-styles-system` - Use platform type system: iOS 11 Dynamic Type styles / Material 5 type roles (display, headline, title, body, label) (HIG, MD)
122	- `weight-hierarchy` - Use font-weight to reinforce hierarchy: Bold headings (600–700), Regular body (400), Medium labels (500) (MD)
123	- `color-semantic` - Define semantic color tokens (primary, secondary, error, surface, on-surface) not raw hex in components (Material color system)
124	- `color-dark-mode` - Dark mode uses desaturated / lighter tonal variants, not inverted colors; test contrast separately (HIG, MD)
125	- `color-accessible-pairs` - Foreground/background pairs must meet 4.5:1 (AA) or 7:1 (AAA); use tools to verify (WCAG, MD)
126	- `color-not-decorative-only` - Functional color (error red, success green) must include icon/text; avoid color-only meaning (HIG, MD)
127	- `truncation-strategy` - Prefer wrapping over truncation; when truncating use ellipsis and provide full text via tooltip/expand (Apple HIG)
128	- `letter-spacing` - Respect default letter-spacing per platform; avoid tight tracking on body text (HIG, MD)
129	- `number-tabular` - Use tabular/monospaced figures for data columns, prices, and timers to prevent layout shift
130	- `whitespace-balance` - Use whitespace intentionally to group related items and separate sections; avoid visual clutter (Apple HIG)
131	- `heading-line-balance` - Use balanced wrapping on short headings as a progressive, user-agent-controlled heuristic; keep natural wrapping readable and never force final words together with blanket nonbreaking spaces
132	- `long-token-wrapping` - Let URLs, IDs, and user content reflow with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` and a shrinkable flex/grid text child; do not apply `word-break: break-all` to normal prose
133	
134	### 7. Animation (MEDIUM)
135	
136	- `duration-timing` - Choose shared motion tokens by distance, complexity, platform, and user context; test that feedback remains responsive instead of treating one duration range as universal
137	- `transform-performance` - Use transform/opacity only; avoid animating width/height/top/left
138	- `loading-states` - Match feedback to the expected wait and platform/component guidance; avoid both flashing indicators for near-instant work and unexplained long waits
139	- `excessive-motion` - Animate 1-2 key elements per view max
140	- `easing` - Use deceleration when arriving, acceleration when leaving, and linear motion for genuinely constant-rate progress or rotation
141	- `motion-meaning` - Every animation must express a cause-effect relationship, not just be decorative (Apple HIG)
142	- `state-transition` - State changes (hover / active / expanded / collapsed / modal) should animate smoothly, not snap
143	- `continuity` - Page/screen transitions should maintain spatial continuity (shared element, directional slide) (Apple HIG)
144	- `parallax-subtle` - Use parallax sparingly; must respect reduced-motion and not cause disorientation (Apple HIG)
145	- `spring-physics` - Prefer spring/physics-based curves over linear or cubic-bezier for natural feel (Apple HIG fluid animations)
146	- `exit-faster-than-enter` - Exit animations shorter than enter (~60–70% of enter duration) to feel responsive (MD motion)
147	- `stagger-sequence` - Stagger list/grid item entrance by 30–50ms per item; avoid all-at-once or too-slow reveals (MD)
148	- `shared-element-transition` - Use shared element / hero transitions for visual continuity between screens (MD, HIG)
149	- `interruptible` - Animations must be interruptible; user tap/gesture cancels in-progress animation immediately (Apple HIG)
150	- `no-blocking-animation` - Never block user input during an animation; UI must stay interactive (Apple HIG)
151	- `fade-crossfade` - Use crossfade for content replacement within the same container (MD)
152	- `scale-feedback` - Subtle scale (0.95–1.05) on press for tappable cards/buttons; restore on release (HIG, MD)
153	- `gesture-feedback` - Drag, swipe, and pinch must provide real-time visual response tracking the finger (MD Motion)
154	- `hierarchy-motion` - Use translate/scale direction to express hierarchy: enter from below = deeper, exit upward = back (MD)
155	- `motion-consistency` - Unify duration/easing tokens globally; all animations share the same rhythm and feel
156	- `opacity-threshold` - Fading elements should not linger below opacity 0.2; either fade fully or remain visible
157	- `modal-motion` - Modals/sheets should animate from their trigger source (scale+fade or slide-in) for spatial context (HIG, MD)
158	- `navigation-direction` - Forward navigation animates left/up; backward animates right/down — keep direction logically consistent (HIG)
159	- `layout-shift-avoid` - Animations must not cause layout reflow or CLS; use transform for position changes
160	- `cancellable-state-transitions` - Rapid state changes must cancel/replace prior micro-interactions safely, set the new final state explicitly, and never depend on an animation-end event for correctness
161	
162	### 8. Forms & Feedback (MEDIUM)
163	
164	- `input-labels` - Visible label per input (not placeholder-only)
165	- `error-placement` - Show a specific error below the related field and connect it with aria-describedby
166	- `submit-feedback` - Loading then success/error state on submit
167	- `required-indicators` - Mark required fields (e.g. asterisk)
168	- `empty-states` - Helpful message and action when no content
169	- `toast-dismiss` - Auto-dismiss toasts in 3-5s
170	- `confirmation-dialogs` - Confirm before destructive actions
171	- `input-helper-text` - Provide persistent helper text below complex inputs, not just placeholder (Material Design)
172	- `disabled-states` - Disabled elements use reduced opacity (0.38–0.5) + cursor change + semantic attribute (MD)
173	- `progressive-disclosure` - Reveal complex options progressively; don't overwhelm users upfront (Apple HIG)
174	- `inline-validation` - Validate on blur (not keystroke); show error only after user finishes input (MD)
175	- `input-type-keyboard` - Use semantic input types (email, tel, number) to trigger the correct mobile keyboard (HIG, MD)
176	- `password-toggle` - Provide show/hide toggle for password fields (MD)
177	- `autofill-support` - Use autocomplete / textContentType attributes so the system can autofill (HIG, MD)
178	- `undo-support` - Allow undo for destructive or bulk actions (e.g. "Undo delete" toast) (Apple HIG)
179	- `success-feedback` - Confirm completed actions with brief visual feedback (checkmark, toast, color flash) (MD)
180	- `error-recovery` - Error messages must include a clear recovery path (retry, edit, help link) (HIG, MD)
181	- `multi-step-progress` - Multi-step flows show step indicator or progress bar; allow back navigation (MD)
182	- `form-autosave` - Long forms should auto-save drafts to prevent data loss on accidental dismissal (Apple HIG)
183	- `sheet-dismiss-confirm` - Confirm before dismissing a sheet/modal with unsaved changes (Apple HIG)
184	- `error-clarity` - Error messages must state cause + how to fix (not just "Invalid input") (HIG, MD)
185	- `field-grouping` - Group related fields logically (fieldset/legend or visual grouping) (MD)
186	- `read-only-distinction` - Read-only state should be visually and semantically different from disabled (MD)
187	- `focus-management` - After failed submission with multiple errors, focus the error summary; without a summary, focus the first invalid field
188	- `error-summary` - Put a focusable summary at the top after failed submit, link each item to its invalid field, and retain inline field errors
189	- `touch-friendly-input` - Mobile input height ≥44px to meet touch target requirements (Apple HIG)
190	- `destructive-emphasis` - Destructive actions use semantic danger color (red) and are visually separated from primary actions (HIG, MD)
191	- `toast-accessibility` - Toasts must not steal focus; use aria-live="polite" for screen reader announcement (WCAG)
192	- `aria-live-errors` - Form errors use aria-live region or role="alert" to notify screen readers (WCAG)
193	- `contrast-feedback` - Error and success state colors must meet 4.5:1 contrast ratio (WCAG, MD)
194	- `timeout-feedback` - Request timeout must show clear feedback with retry option (MD)
195	
196	### 9. Navigation Patterns (HIGH)
197	
198	- `bottom-nav-limit` - Bottom navigation max 5 items; use labels with icons (Material Design)
199	- `drawer-usage` - Use drawer/sidebar for secondary navigation, not primary actions (Material Design)
200	- `back-behavior` - Back navigation must be predictable and consistent; preserve scroll/state (Apple HIG, MD)
201	- `deep-linking` - All key screens must be reachable via deep link / URL for sharing and notifications (Apple HIG, MD)
202	- `tab-bar-ios` - iOS: use bottom Tab Bar for top-level navigation (Apple HIG)
203	- `top-app-bar-android` - Android: use Top App Bar with navigation icon for primary structure (Material Design)
204	- `nav-label-icon` - Navigation items must have both icon and text label; icon-only nav harms discoverability (MD)
205	- `nav-state-active` - Current location must be visually highlighted (color, weight, indicator) in navigation (HIG, MD)
206	- `nav-hierarchy` - Primary nav (tabs/bottom bar) vs secondary nav (drawer/settings) must be clearly separated (MD)
207	- `modal-escape` - Modals and sheets must offer a clear close/dismiss affordance; swipe-down to dismiss on mobile (Apple HIG)
208	- `search-accessible` - Search must be easily reachable (top bar or tab); provide recent/suggested queries (MD)
209	- `breadcrumb-web` - Web: use breadcrumbs for 3+ level deep hierarchies to aid orientation (MD)
210	- `state-preservation` - Navigating back must restore previous scroll position, filter state, and input (HIG, MD)
211	- `gesture-nav-support` - Support system gesture navigation (iOS swipe-back, Android predictive back) without conflict (HIG, MD)
212	- `tab-badge` - Use badges on nav items sparingly to indicate unread/pending; clear after user visits (HIG, MD)
213	- `overflow-menu` - When actions exceed available space, use overflow/more menu instead of cramming (MD)
214	- `bottom-nav-top-level` - Bottom nav is for top-level screens only; never nest sub-navigation inside it (MD)
215	- `adaptive-navigation` - Large screens (≥1024px) prefer sidebar; small screens use bottom/top nav (Material Adaptive)
216	- `back-stack-integrity` - Never silently reset the navigation stack or unexpectedly jump to home (HIG, MD)
217	- `navigation-consistency` - Navigation placement must stay the same across all pages; don't change by page type
218	- `avoid-mixed-patterns` - Don't mix Tab + Sidebar + Bottom Nav at the same hierarchy level
219	- `modal-vs-navigation` - Modals must not be used for primary navigation flows; they break the user's path (HIG)
220	- `focus-on-route-change` - After page transition, move focus to main content region for screen reader users (WCAG)
221	- `persistent-nav` - Core navigation must remain reachable from deep pages; don't hide it entirely in sub-flows (HIG, MD)
222	- `destructive-nav-separation` - Dangerous actions (delete account, logout) must be visually and spatially separated from normal nav items (HIG, MD)
223	- `empty-nav-state` - When a nav destination is unavailable, explain why instead of silently hiding it (MD)
224	
225	### 10. Charts & Data (LOW)
226	
227	- `chart-type` - Match chart type to data type (trend → line, comparison → bar, proportion → pie/donut)
228	- `color-guidance` - Use accessible color palettes; avoid red/green only pairs for colorblind users (WCAG, MD)
229	- `data-table` - Provide table alternative for accessibility; charts alone are not screen-reader friendly (WCAG)
230	- `pattern-texture` - Supplement color with patterns, textures, or shapes so data is distinguishable without color (WCAG, MD)
231	- `legend-visible` - Always show legend; position near the chart, not detached below a scroll fold (MD)
232	- `tooltip-on-interact` - Provide tooltips/data labels on hover (Web) or tap (mobile) showing exact values (HIG, MD)
233	- `axis-labels` - Label axes with units and readable scale; avoid truncated or rotated labels on mobile
234	- `responsive-chart` - Charts must reflow or simplify on small screens (e.g. horizontal bar instead of vertical, fewer ticks)
235	- `empty-data-state` - Show meaningful empty state when no data exists ("No data yet" + guidance), not a blank chart (MD)
236	- `loading-chart` - Use skeleton or shimmer placeholder while chart data loads; don't show an empty axis frame
237	- `animation-optional` - Chart entrance animations must respect prefers-reduced-motion; data should be readable immediately (HIG)
238	- `large-dataset` - For 1000+ data points, aggregate or sample; provide drill-down for detail instead of rendering all (MD)
239	- `number-formatting` - Use locale-aware formatting for numbers, dates, currencies on axes and labels (HIG, MD)
240	- `touch-target-chart` - Interactive chart elements (points, segments) must have ≥44pt tap area or expand on touch (Apple HIG)
241	- `no-pie-overuse` - Avoid pie/donut for >5 categories; switch to bar chart for clarity
242	- `contrast-data` - Data lines/bars vs background ≥3:1; data text labels ≥4.5:1 (WCAG)
243	- `legend-interactive` - Legends should be clickable to toggle series visibility (MD)
244	- `direct-labeling` - For small datasets, label values directly on the chart to reduce eye travel
245	- `tooltip-keyboard` - Tooltip content must be keyboard-reachable and not rely on hover alone (WCAG)
246	- `sortable-table` - Data tables must support sorting with aria-sort indicating current sort state (WCAG)
247	- `axis-readability` - Axis ticks must not be cramped; maintain readable spacing, auto-skip on small screens
248	- `data-density` - Limit information density per chart to avoid cognitive overload; split into multiple charts if needed
249	- `trend-emphasis` - Emphasize data trends over decoration; avoid heavy gradients/shadows that obscure the data
250	- `gridline-subtle` - Grid lines should be low-contrast (e.g. gray-200) so they don't compete with data
251	- `focusable-elements` - Interactive chart elements (points, bars, slices) must be keyboard-navigable (WCAG)
252	- `screen-reader-summary` - Provide a text summary or aria-label describing the chart's key insight for screen readers (WCAG)
253	- `error-state-chart` - Data load failure must show error message with retry action, not a broken/empty chart
254	- `export-option` - For data-heavy products, offer CSV/image export of chart data
255	- `drill-down-consistency` - Drill-down interactions must maintain a clear back-path and hierarchy breadcrumb
256	- `time-scale-clarity` - Time series charts must clearly label time granularity (day/week/month) and allow switching
257

# Quick Reference — Full Rule Set (all 10 categories)

Load this file when doing a UI review/audit pass, or when you need the full checklist for a category beyond the priority table in SKILL.md. Each rule is also present verbatim in `data/ux-guidelines.csv` / `data/app-interface.csv` and is reachable via `--domain ux` / `--domain web` search — this file is a static index for quick scanning without a search round-trip.

## Quick Reference

### 1. Accessibility (CRITICAL)

- `color-contrast` - Minimum 4.5:1 ratio for normal text (large text 3:1); Material Design
- `focus-states` - Visible focus rings on interactive elements (2–4px; Apple HIG, MD)
- `alt-text` - Descriptive alt text for meaningful images
- `aria-labels` - aria-label for icon-only buttons; accessibilityLabel in native (Apple HIG)
- `icon-context` - Semantics depend on use: decorative icons beside visible text are hidden from the accessibility tree; meaningful icons need a text alternative; icon controls need an accessible name and applicable state
- `keyboard-nav` - Tab order matches visual order; full keyboard support (Apple HIG)
- `form-labels` - Use label with for attribute
- `skip-links` - Skip to main content for keyboard users
- `heading-hierarchy` - Sequential h1→h6, no level skip
- `color-not-only` - Don't convey info by color alone (add icon/text)
- `dynamic-type` - Support system text scaling; avoid truncation as text grows (Apple Dynamic Type, MD)
- `reduced-motion` - Respect prefers-reduced-motion; reduce/disable animations when requested (Apple Reduced Motion API, MD)
- `voiceover-sr` - Meaningful accessibilityLabel/accessibilityHint; logical reading order for VoiceOver/screen readers (Apple HIG, MD)
- `escape-routes` - Provide cancel/back in modals and multi-step flows (Apple HIG)
- `keyboard-shortcuts` - Preserve system and a11y shortcuts; offer keyboard alternatives for drag-and-drop (Apple HIG)
- `focus-not-obscured` - Sticky UI, overlays, and banners must not hide the keyboard-focused control (WCAG 2.2 AA)
- `focus-not-obscured-enhanced` - Keep the entire focused component visible (WCAG 2.2 AAA)
- `focus-appearance` - Verify focus indicator area and 3:1 state contrast; visible focus alone is not enough (WCAG 2.2 AAA)
- `dragging-alternative` - Every author-controlled drag action needs a single-pointer and keyboard alternative (WCAG 2.2 AA)
- `web-target-size` - Web pointer targets need 24×24 CSS px or a documented exception; do not substitute native units (WCAG 2.2 AA)
- `consistent-help` - Repeated help mechanisms stay in the same relative order across a page set (WCAG 2.2 A)
- `redundant-entry` - Reuse information already supplied in the same process unless re-entry is essential (WCAG 2.2 A)
- `accessible-authentication` - Allow password managers and paste; provide a non-cognitive authentication path (WCAG 2.2 Minimum, AA). The Enhanced AAA criterion is not represented in the dataset
- `auto-rotation-controls` - Carousels and moving content need pause/stop controls and must stop on focus or reduced motion (WAI)
- `contextual-live-badge-updates` - Announce a changed count/status as a complete contextual phrase without moving focus; use one appropriate live/status region and atomic updates only when needed

### 2. Touch & Interaction (CRITICAL)

- `touch-target-size` - Min 44×44pt (Apple) / 48×48dp (Material); extend hit area beyond visual bounds if needed
- `touch-spacing` - Minimum 8px/8dp gap between touch targets (Apple HIG, MD)
- `hover-vs-tap` - Use click/tap for primary interactions; don't rely on hover alone
- `loading-buttons` - Disable button during async operations; show spinner or progress
- `error-feedback` - Clear error messages near problem
- `cursor-pointer` - Add cursor-pointer to clickable elements (Web)
- `gesture-conflicts` - Avoid horizontal swipe on main content; prefer vertical scroll
- `tap-delay` - Use touch-action: manipulation to reduce 300ms delay (Web)
- `standard-gestures` - Use platform standard gestures consistently; don't redefine (e.g. swipe-back, pinch-zoom) (Apple HIG)
- `system-gestures` - Don't block system gestures (Control Center, back swipe, etc.) (Apple HIG)
- `press-feedback` - Visual feedback on press (ripple/highlight; MD state layers)
- `haptic-feedback` - Use haptic for confirmations and important actions; avoid overuse (Apple HIG)
- `gesture-alternative` - Don't rely on gesture-only interactions; always provide visible controls for critical actions
- `safe-area-awareness` - Keep primary touch targets away from notch, Dynamic Island, gesture bar and screen edges
- `no-precision-required` - Avoid requiring pixel-perfect taps on small icons or thin edges
- `swipe-clarity` - Swipe actions must show clear affordance or hint (chevron, label, tutorial)
- `drag-threshold` - Use a movement threshold before starting drag to avoid accidental drags

### 3. Performance (HIGH)

- `image-optimization` - Use WebP/AVIF, responsive images (srcset/sizes), lazy load non-critical assets
- `image-dimension` - Declare width/height or use aspect-ratio to prevent layout shift (Core Web Vitals: CLS)
- `font-loading` - Use font-display: swap/optional to avoid invisible text (FOIT); reserve space to reduce layout shift (MD)
- `font-preload` - Preload only critical fonts; avoid overusing preload on every variant
- `critical-css` - Prioritize above-the-fold CSS (inline critical CSS or early-loaded stylesheet)
- `lazy-loading` - Lazy load non-hero components via dynamic import / route-level splitting
- `bundle-splitting` - Split code by route/feature (React Suspense / Next.js dynamic) to reduce initial load and TTI
- `third-party-scripts` - Load third-party scripts async/defer; audit and remove unnecessary ones (MD)
- `reduce-reflows` - Avoid frequent layout reads/writes; batch DOM reads then writes
- `content-jumping` - Reserve space for async content to avoid layout jumps (Core Web Vitals: CLS)
- `lazy-load-below-fold` - Use loading="lazy" for below-the-fold images and heavy media
- `virtualize-lists` - Virtualize lists with 50+ items to improve memory efficiency and scroll performance
- `main-thread-budget` - Keep per-frame work under ~16ms for 60fps; move heavy tasks off main thread (HIG, MD)
- `progressive-loading` - Use skeleton screens / shimmer instead of long blocking spinners for >1s operations (Apple HIG)
- `input-latency` - Keep input latency under ~100ms for taps/scrolls (Material responsiveness standard)
- `tap-feedback-speed` - Provide visual feedback within 100ms of tap (Apple HIG)
- `debounce-throttle` - Use debounce/throttle for high-frequency events (scroll, resize, input)
- `offline-support` - Provide offline state messaging and basic fallback (PWA / mobile)
- `network-fallback` - Offer degraded modes for slow networks (lower-res images, fewer animations)

### 4. Style Selection (HIGH)

- `style-match` - Match style to product type (use `--design-system` for recommendations)
- `consistency` - Use same style across all pages
- `no-emoji-icons` - Use SVG icons (Heroicons, Lucide), not emojis
- `color-palette-from-product` - Choose palette from product/industry (search `--domain color`)
- `effects-match-style` - Shadows, blur, radius aligned with chosen style (glass / flat / clay etc.)
- `platform-adaptive` - Respect platform idioms (iOS HIG vs Material): navigation, controls, typography, motion
- `state-clarity` - Make hover/pressed/disabled states visually distinct while staying on-style (Material state layers)
- `elevation-consistent` - Use a consistent elevation/shadow scale for cards, sheets, modals; avoid random shadow values
- `dark-mode-pairing` - Design light/dark variants together to keep brand, contrast, and style consistent
- `icon-style-consistent` - Use one icon set/visual language (stroke width, corner radius) across the product
- `system-controls` - Prefer native/system controls over fully custom ones; only customize when branding requires it (Apple HIG)
- `blur-purpose` - Use blur to indicate background dismissal (modals, sheets), not as decoration (Apple HIG)
- `primary-action` - Each screen should have only one primary CTA; secondary actions visually subordinate (Apple HIG)

### 5. Layout & Responsive (HIGH)

- `viewport-meta` - width=device-width initial-scale=1 (never disable zoom)
- `mobile-first` - Design mobile-first, then scale up to tablet and desktop
- `breakpoint-consistency` - Use systematic breakpoints (e.g. 375 / 768 / 1024 / 1440)
- `readable-font-size` - Minimum 16px body text on mobile (avoids iOS auto-zoom)
- `line-length-control` - Mobile 35–60 chars per line; desktop 60–75 chars
- `horizontal-scroll` - No horizontal scroll on mobile; ensure content fits viewport width
- `spacing-scale` - Use 4pt/8dp incremental spacing system (Material Design)
- `touch-density` - Keep component spacing comfortable for touch: not cramped, not causing mis-taps
- `container-width` - Consistent max-width on desktop (max-w-6xl / 7xl)
- `z-index-management` - Define layered z-index scale (e.g. 0 / 10 / 20 / 40 / 100 / 1000)
- `fixed-element-offset` - Fixed navbar/bottom bar must reserve safe padding for underlying content
- `scroll-behavior` - Avoid nested scroll regions that interfere with the main scroll experience
- `viewport-units` - Prefer min-h-dvh over 100vh on mobile
- `orientation-support` - Keep layout readable and operable in landscape mode
- `content-priority` - Show core content first on mobile; fold or hide secondary content
- `visual-hierarchy` - Establish hierarchy via size, spacing, contrast — not color alone
- `compact-label-overflow` - Choose badge, status tag, filter chip, or removable value from its semantics; keep essential labels available and disclose unavoidable truncation to pointer and keyboard users
- `chip-collection-reflow` - Wrap the collection before shrinking labels; make a `+n` overflow summary an operable disclosure instead of hiding values

### 6. Typography & Color (MEDIUM)

- `line-height` - Use 1.5-1.75 for body text
- `line-length` - Limit to 65-75 characters per line
- `font-pairing` - Match heading/body font personalities
- `font-scale` - Consistent type scale (e.g. 12 14 16 18 24 32)
- `contrast-readability` - Darker text on light backgrounds (e.g. slate-900 on white)
- `text-styles-system` - Use platform type system: iOS 11 Dynamic Type styles / Material 5 type roles (display, headline, title, body, label) (HIG, MD)
- `weight-hierarchy` - Use font-weight to reinforce hierarchy: Bold headings (600–700), Regular body (400), Medium labels (500) (MD)
- `color-semantic` - Define semantic color tokens (primary, secondary, error, surface, on-surface) not raw hex in components (Material color system)
- `color-dark-mode` - Dark mode uses desaturated / lighter tonal variants, not inverted colors; test contrast separately (HIG, MD)
- `color-accessible-pairs` - Foreground/background pairs must meet 4.5:1 (AA) or 7:1 (AAA); use tools to verify (WCAG, MD)
- `color-not-decorative-only` - Functional color (error red, success green) must include icon/text; avoid color-only meaning (HIG, MD)
- `truncation-strategy` - Prefer wrapping over truncation; when truncating use ellipsis and provide full text via tooltip/expand (Apple HIG)
- `letter-spacing` - Respect default letter-spacing per platform; avoid tight tracking on body text (HIG, MD)
- `number-tabular` - Use tabular/monospaced figures for data columns, prices, and timers to prevent layout shift
- `whitespace-balance` - Use whitespace intentionally to group related items and separate sections; avoid visual clutter (Apple HIG)
- `heading-line-balance` - Use balanced wrapping on short headings as a progressive, user-agent-controlled heuristic; keep natural wrapping readable and never force final words together with blanket nonbreaking spaces
- `long-token-wrapping` - Let URLs, IDs, and user content reflow with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` and a shrinkable flex/grid text child; do not apply `word-break: break-all` to normal prose

### 7. Animation (MEDIUM)

- `duration-timing` - Choose shared motion tokens by distance, complexity, platform, and user context; test that feedback remains responsive instead of treating one duration range as universal
- `transform-performance` - Use transform/opacity only; avoid animating width/height/top/left
- `loading-states` - Match feedback to the expected wait and platform/component guidance; avoid both flashing indicators for near-instant work and unexplained long waits
- `excessive-motion` - Animate 1-2 key elements per view max
- `easing` - Use deceleration when arriving, acceleration when leaving, and linear motion for genuinely constant-rate progress or rotation
- `motion-meaning` - Every animation must express a cause-effect relationship, not just be decorative (Apple HIG)
- `state-transition` - State changes (hover / active / expanded / collapsed / modal) should animate smoothly, not snap
- `continuity` - Page/screen transitions should maintain spatial continuity (shared element, directional slide) (Apple HIG)
- `parallax-subtle` - Use parallax sparingly; must respect reduced-motion and not cause disorientation (Apple HIG)
- `spring-physics` - Prefer spring/physics-based curves over linear or cubic-bezier for natural feel (Apple HIG fluid animations)
- `exit-faster-than-enter` - Exit animations shorter than enter (~60–70% of enter duration) to feel responsive (MD motion)
- `stagger-sequence` - Stagger list/grid item entrance by 30–50ms per item; avoid all-at-once or too-slow reveals (MD)
- `shared-element-transition` - Use shared element / hero transitions for visual continuity between screens (MD, HIG)
- `interruptible` - Animations must be interruptible; user tap/gesture cancels in-progress animation immediately (Apple HIG)
- `no-blocking-animation` - Never block user input during an animation; UI must stay interactive (Apple HIG)
- `fade-crossfade` - Use crossfade for content replacement within the same container (MD)
- `scale-feedback` - Subtle scale (0.95–1.05) on press for tappable cards/buttons; restore on release (HIG, MD)
- `gesture-feedback` - Drag, swipe, and pinch must provide real-time visual response tracking the finger (MD Motion)
- `hierarchy-motion` - Use translate/scale direction to express hierarchy: enter from below = deeper, exit upward = back (MD)
- `motion-consistency` - Unify duration/easing tokens globally; all animations share the same rhythm and feel
- `opacity-threshold` - Fading elements should not linger below opacity 0.2; either fade fully or remain visible
- `modal-motion` - Modals/sheets should animate from their trigger source (scale+fade or slide-in) for spatial context (HIG, MD)
- `navigation-direction` - Forward navigation animates left/up; backward animates right/down — keep direction logically consistent (HIG)
- `layout-shift-avoid` - Animations must not cause layout reflow or CLS; use transform for position changes
- `cancellable-state-transitions` - Rapid state changes must cancel/replace prior micro-interactions safely, set the new final state explicitly, and never depend on an animation-end event for correctness

### 8. Forms & Feedback (MEDIUM)

- `input-labels` - Visible label per input (not placeholder-only)
- `error-placement` - Show a specific error below the related field and connect it with aria-describedby
- `submit-feedback` - Loading then success/error state on submit
- `required-indicators` - Mark required fields (e.g. asterisk)
- `empty-states` - Helpful message and action when no content
- `toast-dismiss` - Auto-dismiss toasts in 3-5s
- `confirmation-dialogs` - Confirm before destructive actions
- `input-helper-text` - Provide persistent helper text below complex inputs, not just placeholder (Material Design)
- `disabled-states` - Disabled elements use reduced opacity (0.38–0.5) + cursor change + semantic attribute (MD)
- `progressive-disclosure` - Reveal complex options progressively; don't overwhelm users upfront (Apple HIG)
- `inline-validation` - Validate on blur (not keystroke); show error only after user finishes input (MD)
- `input-type-keyboard` - Use semantic input types (email, tel, number) to trigger the correct mobile keyboard (HIG, MD)
- `password-toggle` - Provide show/hide toggle for password fields (MD)
- `autofill-support` - Use autocomplete / textContentType attributes so the system can autofill (HIG, MD)
- `undo-support` - Allow undo for destructive or bulk actions (e.g. "Undo delete" toast) (Apple HIG)
- `success-feedback` - Confirm completed actions with brief visual feedback (checkmark, toast, color flash) (MD)
- `error-recovery` - Error messages must include a clear recovery path (retry, edit, help link) (HIG, MD)
- `multi-step-progress` - Multi-step flows show step indicator or progress bar; allow back navigation (MD)
- `form-autosave` - Long forms should auto-save drafts to prevent data loss on accidental dismissal (Apple HIG)
- `sheet-dismiss-confirm` - Confirm before dismissing a sheet/modal with unsaved changes (Apple HIG)
- `error-clarity` - Error messages must state cause + how to fix (not just "Invalid input") (HIG, MD)
- `field-grouping` - Group related fields logically (fieldset/legend or visual grouping) (MD)
- `read-only-distinction` - Read-only state should be visually and semantically different from disabled (MD)
- `focus-management` - After failed submission with multiple errors, focus the error summary; without a summary, focus the first invalid field
- `error-summary` - Put a focusable summary at the top after failed submit, link each item to its invalid field, and retain inline field errors
- `touch-friendly-input` - Mobile input height ≥44px to meet touch target requirements (Apple HIG)
- `destructive-emphasis` - Destructive actions use semantic danger color (red) and are visually separated from primary actions (HIG, MD)
- `toast-accessibility` - Toasts must not steal focus; use aria-live="polite" for screen reader announcement (WCAG)
- `aria-live-errors` - Form errors use aria-live region or role="alert" to notify screen readers (WCAG)
- `contrast-feedback` - Error and success state colors must meet 4.5:1 contrast ratio (WCAG, MD)
- `timeout-feedback` - Request timeout must show clear feedback with retry option (MD)

### 9. Navigation Patterns (HIGH)

- `bottom-nav-limit` - Bottom navigation max 5 items; use labels with icons (Material Design)
- `drawer-usage` - Use drawer/sidebar for secondary navigation, not primary actions (Material Design)
- `back-behavior` - Back navigation must be predictable and consistent; preserve scroll/state (Apple HIG, MD)
- `deep-linking` - All key screens must be reachable via deep link / URL for sharing and notifications (Apple HIG, MD)
- `tab-bar-ios` - iOS: use bottom Tab Bar for top-level navigation (Apple HIG)
- `top-app-bar-android` - Android: use Top App Bar with navigation icon for primary structure (Material Design)
- `nav-label-icon` - Navigation items must have both icon and text label; icon-only nav harms discoverability (MD)
- `nav-state-active` - Current location must be visually highlighted (color, weight, indicator) in navigation (HIG, MD)
- `nav-hierarchy` - Primary nav (tabs/bottom bar) vs secondary nav (drawer/settings) must be clearly separated (MD)
- `modal-escape` - Modals and sheets must offer a clear close/dismiss affordance; swipe-down to dismiss on mobile (Apple HIG)
- `search-accessible` - Search must be easily reachable (top bar or tab); provide recent/suggested queries (MD)
- `breadcrumb-web` - Web: use breadcrumbs for 3+ level deep hierarchies to aid orientation (MD)
- `state-preservation` - Navigating back must restore previous scroll position, filter state, and input (HIG, MD)
- `gesture-nav-support` - Support system gesture navigation (iOS swipe-back, Android predictive back) without conflict (HIG, MD)
- `tab-badge` - Use badges on nav items sparingly to indicate unread/pending; clear after user visits (HIG, MD)
- `overflow-menu` - When actions exceed available space, use overflow/more menu instead of cramming (MD)
- `bottom-nav-top-level` - Bottom nav is for top-level screens only; never nest sub-navigation inside it (MD)
- `adaptive-navigation` - Large screens (≥1024px) prefer sidebar; small screens use bottom/top nav (Material Adaptive)
- `back-stack-integrity` - Never silently reset the navigation stack or unexpectedly jump to home (HIG, MD)
- `navigation-consistency` - Navigation placement must stay the same across all pages; don't change by page type
- `avoid-mixed-patterns` - Don't mix Tab + Sidebar + Bottom Nav at the same hierarchy level
- `modal-vs-navigation` - Modals must not be used for primary navigation flows; they break the user's path (HIG)
- `focus-on-route-change` - After page transition, move focus to main content region for screen reader users (WCAG)
- `persistent-nav` - Core navigation must remain reachable from deep pages; don't hide it entirely in sub-flows (HIG, MD)
- `destructive-nav-separation` - Dangerous actions (delete account, logout) must be visually and spatially separated from normal nav items (HIG, MD)
- `empty-nav-state` - When a nav destination is unavailable, explain why instead of silently hiding it (MD)

### 10. Charts & Data (LOW)

- `chart-type` - Match chart type to data type (trend → line, comparison → bar, proportion → pie/donut)
- `color-guidance` - Use accessible color palettes; avoid red/green only pairs for colorblind users (WCAG, MD)
- `data-table` - Provide table alternative for accessibility; charts alone are not screen-reader friendly (WCAG)
- `pattern-texture` - Supplement color with patterns, textures, or shapes so data is distinguishable without color (WCAG, MD)
- `legend-visible` - Always show legend; position near the chart, not detached below a scroll fold (MD)
- `tooltip-on-interact` - Provide tooltips/data labels on hover (Web) or tap (mobile) showing exact values (HIG, MD)
- `axis-labels` - Label axes with units and readable scale; avoid truncated or rotated labels on mobile
- `responsive-chart` - Charts must reflow or simplify on small screens (e.g. horizontal bar instead of vertical, fewer ticks)
- `empty-data-state` - Show meaningful empty state when no data exists ("No data yet" + guidance), not a blank chart (MD)
- `loading-chart` - Use skeleton or shimmer placeholder while chart data loads; don't show an empty axis frame
- `animation-optional` - Chart entrance animations must respect prefers-reduced-motion; data should be readable immediately (HIG)
- `large-dataset` - For 1000+ data points, aggregate or sample; provide drill-down for detail instead of rendering all (MD)
- `number-formatting` - Use locale-aware formatting for numbers, dates, currencies on axes and labels (HIG, MD)
- `touch-target-chart` - Interactive chart elements (points, segments) must have ≥44pt tap area or expand on touch (Apple HIG)
- `no-pie-overuse` - Avoid pie/donut for >5 categories; switch to bar chart for clarity
- `contrast-data` - Data lines/bars vs background ≥3:1; data text labels ≥4.5:1 (WCAG)
- `legend-interactive` - Legends should be clickable to toggle series visibility (MD)
- `direct-labeling` - For small datasets, label values directly on the chart to reduce eye travel
- `tooltip-keyboard` - Tooltip content must be keyboard-reachable and not rely on hover alone (WCAG)
- `sortable-table` - Data tables must support sorting with aria-sort indicating current sort state (WCAG)
- `axis-readability` - Axis ticks must not be cramped; maintain readable spacing, auto-skip on small screens
- `data-density` - Limit information density per chart to avoid cognitive overload; split into multiple charts if needed
- `trend-emphasis` - Emphasize data trends over decoration; avoid heavy gradients/shadows that obscure the data
- `gridline-subtle` - Grid lines should be low-contrast (e.g. gray-200) so they don't compete with data
- `focusable-elements` - Interactive chart elements (points, bars, slices) must be keyboard-navigable (WCAG)
- `screen-reader-summary` - Provide a text summary or aria-label describing the chart's key insight for screen readers (WCAG)
- `error-state-chart` - Data load failure must show error message with retry action, not a broken/empty chart
- `export-option` - For data-heavy products, offer CSV/image export of chart data
- `drill-down-consistency` - Drill-down interactions must maintain a clear back-path and hierarchy breadcrumb
- `time-scale-clarity` - Time series charts must clearly label time granularity (day/week/month) and allow switching

# UI/UX Pro Max - Design Intelligence

Searchable local UI/UX guidance: 79 searchable styles (50 active), 192 product palettes and exact reasoning profiles, 74 font pairings, 119 UX guidelines, 105 curated icons, 17 GSAP presets, 25 chart types, and 22 technology stacks.

## When to Apply

Use this Skill when the task involves **UI structure, visual design decisions, interaction patterns, or user experience quality control**: designing new pages, creating/refactoring UI components, choosing color/typography/spacing/layout systems, reviewing UI for UX/accessibility/consistency, implementing navigation/animation/responsive behavior, or improving perceived quality and usability.

Skip it for pure backend logic, API/database design, non-visual performance work, infrastructure/DevOps, or non-visual scripts — unless the task changes how something **looks, feels, moves, or is interacted with**.

## Rule Categories by Priority

*Follow priority 1→10 to decide which category to focus on first; use `--domain <Domain>` to query full details. The full rule text for every category lives in `references/quick-reference.md` — read it on demand rather than loading it every time.*

| Priority | Category | Impact | Domain | Key Checks (Must Have) | Anti-Patterns (Avoid) |
|----------|----------|--------|--------|------------------------|------------------------|
| 1 | Accessibility | CRITICAL | `ux` | Contrast 4.5:1, Alt text, Keyboard nav, Aria-labels | Removing focus rings, Icon-only buttons without labels |
| 2 | Touch & Interaction | CRITICAL | `ux` | Min size 44×44px, 8px+ spacing, Loading feedback | Reliance on hover only, Instant state changes (0ms) |
| 3 | Performance | HIGH | `ux` | WebP/AVIF, Lazy loading, Reserve space (CLS < 0.1) | Layout thrashing, Cumulative Layout Shift |
| 4 | Style Selection | HIGH | `style`, `product` | Match product type, Consistency, SVG icons (no emoji) | Mixing flat & skeuomorphic randomly, Emoji as icons |
| 5 | Layout & Responsive | HIGH | `ux` | Mobile-first breakpoints, Viewport meta, No horizontal scroll | Horizontal scroll, Fixed px container widths, Disable zoom |
| 6 | Typography & Color | MEDIUM | `typography`, `color` | Base 16px, Line-height 1.5, Semantic color tokens | Text < 12px body, Gray-on-gray, Raw hex in components |
| 7 | Animation | MEDIUM | `ux`, `gsap` | Context-aware timing, Motion conveys meaning, Spatial continuity | One duration for every transition, Animating width/height, No reduced-motion |
| 8 | Forms & Feedback | MEDIUM | `ux` | Visible labels, Error near field, Helper text, Progressive disclosure | Placeholder-only label, Errors only at top, Overwhelm upfront |
| 9 | Navigation Patterns | HIGH | `ux` | Predictable back, Bottom nav ≤5, Deep linking | Overloaded nav, Broken back behavior, No deep links |
| 10 | Charts & Data | LOW | `chart` | Legends, Tooltips, Accessible colors | Relying on color alone to convey meaning |

For the full rule list per category (all 119 UX guidelines with rationale), read `references/quick-reference.md`. For app-specific polish rules (icons, touch feedback, dark mode contrast, safe areas) and the canonical pre-delivery checklist, read `references/pro-rules.md`.

1	# Common Rules for Professional UI + Pre-Delivery Checklist
2	
3	Load this file before final delivery of native/mobile app UI (iOS/Android/React Native/Flutter), or when the user reports the UI "doesn't look professional" and the cause isn't obvious from the priority table in SKILL.md.
4	
5	**Scope notice:** everything below targets native/mobile app UI. For web/desktop interaction patterns, use `references/quick-reference.md` (stack-agnostic) instead — these tables assume touch targets, safe areas, and platform gesture conventions that don't apply 1:1 to desktop web.
6	
7	These are frequently overlooked issues that make UI look unprofessional.
8	
9	## Icons & Visual Elements
10	
11	| Rule | Standard | Avoid | Why It Matters |
12	|------|----------|--------|----------------|
13	| **No Emoji as Structural Icons** | Use vector-based icons (e.g., Lucide, react-native-vector-icons, @expo/vector-icons). | Using emojis (🎨 🚀 ⚙️) for navigation, settings, or system controls. | Emojis are font-dependent, inconsistent across platforms, and cannot be controlled via design tokens. |
14	| **Vector-Only Assets** | Use SVG or platform vector icons that scale cleanly and support theming. | Raster PNG icons that blur or pixelate. | Ensures scalability, crisp rendering, and dark/light mode adaptability. |
15	| **Contextual Semantics** | Choose semantics from use, not glyph: hide decorative icons beside visible text from the accessibility tree; give meaningful standalone icons a text alternative; give icon controls an accessible name and expose selected/pressed/expanded state when applicable. | Treating one icon name as permanently decorative, meaningful, or interactive. | The same glyph can serve different purposes in different components. |
16	| **Stable Interaction States** | Use color, opacity, or elevation transitions for press states without changing layout bounds. | Layout-shifting transforms that move surrounding content or trigger visual jitter. | Prevents unstable interactions and preserves smooth motion/perceived quality on mobile. |
17	| **Correct Brand Logos** | Use official brand assets and follow their usage guidelines (spacing, color, clear space). | Guessing logo paths, recoloring unofficially, or modifying proportions. | Prevents brand misuse and ensures legal/platform compliance. |
18	| **Consistent Icon Sizing** | Define icon sizes as design tokens (e.g., icon-sm, icon-md = 24pt, icon-lg). | Mixing arbitrary values like 20pt / 24pt / 28pt randomly. | Maintains rhythm and visual hierarchy across the interface. |
19	| **Stroke Consistency** | Use a consistent stroke width within the same visual layer (e.g., 1.5px or 2px). | Mixing thick and thin stroke styles arbitrarily. | Inconsistent strokes reduce perceived polish and cohesion. |
20	| **Filled vs Outline Discipline** | Use one icon style per hierarchy level. | Mixing filled and outline icons at the same hierarchy level. | Maintains semantic clarity and stylistic coherence. |
21	| **Touch Target Minimum** | Use at least 44pt on iOS and 48dp on Android; expand the hit area when the visual icon is smaller. | Small icons without expanded tap area, or one unit reused across platforms. | Matches platform-specific target guidance. |
22	| **Icon Alignment** | Align icons to text baseline and maintain consistent padding. | Misaligned icons or inconsistent spacing around them. | Prevents subtle visual imbalance that reduces perceived quality. |
